manifest.name: 6W6
manifest.about: Drum machine voice set ported from athousanddetails' schwung-6W6, as an MPC/Force VST2 instrument.

versions.notes:
Drum machine voice set ported from athousanddetails' schwung-6W6, as an MPC/Force VST2 instrument.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r 6W6-1.2.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/6W6-1.2.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/athousanddetails - VST - 6W6/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **6W6** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

versions.notes:
# Airwindows for MPC and Force 0.1.0

The first eleven collections of Chris Johnson's Airwindows effects as native MPC OS plugins. One plugin per Airwindows category;
each holds every effect in that category, with its own panel, Q-Link badges and a MANUAL tab. See the README for the approach.

| Plugin | Models |
|---|---|
| AW Tape | 12 |
| AW Distortion | 15 |
| AW Saturation | 20 |
| AW Dynamics | 35 |
| AW Filter | 54 |
| AW Reverb | 42 |
| AW Ambience (includes Echojam) | 26 |
| AW Consoles | 50 |
| AW Console Strips (4 pages) | 8 |
| AW Utility | 38 |
| AW Effects | 29 |

The other 13 collections follow in later releases.

## Which zip

- `*-mpc-armv7.zip`: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61 (first-generation, 32-bit).
- `*-mpc-aarch64.zip`: MPC Live III and other second-generation devices (MPC OS 3.x).

Each zip is one plugin with its own `install.sh` and `uninstall.sh` (it stops MPC, backs up `MPC.settings`, and restarts MPC).

## Requirements

- An MPC OS standalone device of the matching generation, with **root shell access** (SSH). Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- MPC OS 3.x (the skins use features older versions lack).
- Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r AW-Tape-0.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/AW-Tape-0.1.0/install.sh`
3. Add the plugin to a track from the plugin browser (Insert effects).

## Tested

The zips' own `install.sh` has been run on a Force (armv7) and an MPC Live III (aarch64) by the author.

## Known limits

- No CPU benchmark has been run.
- Parameter positions may still change in a later release, which would break saved projects that use these plugins.
- Models with no upstream manual (for example Spiral3, Weave, PunchyDeluxe, ConsoleX2 and ConsoleX3) show a short note.

Airwindows is by Chris Johnson (MIT), ported via airwin2rack. This project is MIT licensed.

# Airwindows for MPC and Force 0.1.0

The first eleven collections of Chris Johnson's Airwindows effects as native MPC OS plugins. One plugin per Airwindows category;
each holds every effect in that category, with its own panel, Q-Link badges and a MANUAL tab. See the README for the approach.

| Plugin | Models |
|---|---|
| AW Tape | 12 |
| AW Distortion | 15 |
| AW Saturation | 20 |
| AW Dynamics | 35 |
| AW Filter | 54 |
| AW Reverb | 42 |
| AW Ambience (includes Echojam) | 26 |
| AW Consoles | 50 |
| AW Console Strips (4 pages) | 8 |
| AW Utility | 38 |
| AW Effects | 29 |

The other 13 collections follow in later releases.

## Which zip

- `*-mpc-armv7.zip`: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61 (first-generation, 32-bit).
- `*-mpc-aarch64.zip`: MPC Live III and other second-generation devices (MPC OS 3.x).

Each zip is one plugin with its own `install.sh` and `uninstall.sh` (it stops MPC, backs up `MPC.settings`, and restarts MPC).

## Requirements

- An MPC OS standalone device of the matching generation, with **root shell access** (SSH). Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- MPC OS 3.x (the skins use features older versions lack).
- Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r AW-Tape-0.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/AW-Tape-0.1.0/install.sh`
3. Add the plugin to a track from the plugin browser (Insert effects).

## Tested

The zips' own `install.sh` has been run on a Force (armv7) and an MPC Live III (aarch64) by the author.

## Known limits

- No CPU benchmark has been run.
- Parameter positions may still change in a later release, which would break saved projects that use these plugins.
- Models with no upstream manual (for example Spiral3, Weave, PunchyDeluxe, ConsoleX2 and ConsoleX3) show a short note.

Airwindows is by Chris Johnson (MIT), ported via airwin2rack. This project is MIT licensed.

manifest.about: Korg MS-10/MS-20 style mono synth with a patch bay, an ESP section and both MS filters.

versions.notes:
Korg MS-10/MS-20 style mono synth with a patch bay, an ESP section and both MS filters.

## What's new in 1.1.1

Built on sd88me's fixed wrapper ([mpc-vst-plugins#499](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins/discussions/499)): on track edit → automation, the physical Q-Links move this plugin's parameters again (before, they didn't move or snapped straight back). Controls that change others, such as a preset, still redraw the screen. Nothing else changed: same parameters, sound and screen, and saved projects open as before.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r SYN-Aphex-1.1.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/SYN-Aphex-1.1.1/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/Filliformes - VST - [SYN] Aphex/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **[SYN] Aphex** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

Clementine-XT 0.9.5: a new look and a tidier Sound row.

# Clementine-XT 0.9.0

Wavetable instrument modelled on the Microwave XT architecture, for MPC OS.

A native MPC OS plugin (instrument) with its own MPC screen skin, loaded by MPC's built-in plugin host.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Clementine-XT-0.9.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Clementine-XT-0.9.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/sd88me - VST - Clementine-XT/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Your own files go in `ROMS/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/sd88me - VST - Clementine-XT/`); the installer keeps them when you upgrade and uninstall, and moves them there from the old `/sdcard/vst` location if you had installed the plugin that way.

Then add **Clementine-XT** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Clementine-XT-0.9.0/uninstall.sh` removes the plugin folder and the plugin-list entry (it also stops and
restarts MPC). Projects that use the plugin will load without it. Files you added yourself are kept.

## Install by hand

1. Copy `portable/sd88me - VST - Clementine-XT/` to `/sdcard/Synths/sd88me - VST - Clementine-XT/`. It holds `clementine_xt.so`, `plugin-meta.xml`, `version.xml`, `Plugin Skins/`
   and the data:
2. Stop MPC: `systemctl stop acvs` (`systemctl stop inmusic-mpc` on a Hakai-enabled system)
3. Back up the settings file, `MPC.settings` (on a Force: `/media/az01-internal/Settings/MPC/MPC.settings`).
4. In `MPC.settings`, inside `<VALUE name="pluginList-arm"><KNOWNPLUGINS>`, add the line from `plugin-meta.xml` with
   `%payload-path%` replaced by `/sdcard/Synths`. If there is no `pluginList-arm` value yet, add one just before `</PROPERTIES>`:
   ```xml
   <VALUE name="pluginList-arm">
     <KNOWNPLUGINS>
       (the line from plugin-meta.xml)
     </KNOWNPLUGINS>
   </VALUE>
   ```
5. Start MPC: `systemctl start acvs` (`inmusic-mpc` on Hakai). If MPC shows default settings, restore your backup (the XML was malformed).

Edit `MPC.settings` only while MPC is stopped: MPC can save its own copy over a change made while it runs. Tools that
rebuild the whole plugin list from the plugin folders in `Synths` keep this plugin, because it is such a folder.

versions.notes:
Clif Tape 0.2.0 — stereo tape colour and texture for Windows, macOS, Linux and Force / MPC.

Ready-built VST3 downloads for Windows x64, Mac Intel + Apple Silicon, and Linux x86-64. The desktop editions share the cliff artwork, white knobs, four pages, 15 presets and 18 automatable parameters. No compiling required.

Tape EQ profiles, saturation, Wow and Flutter, Crackle, Spread, independent Noise and Mechanical textures, plus Digital filtering and DEGRADE. Silence Gate fades Crackle, Noise and Mechanical when input becomes silent; it leaves the music signal alone.

[Downloads and screen previews](https://github.com/MagicStino/Clif-Tape#download--ready-to-play) · [Installation](https://github.com/MagicStino/Clif-Tape/blob/main/INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](https://github.com/MagicStino/Clif-Tape/blob/main/USAGE.md)

Desktop ZIPs: extract the complete ClifTape.vst3 bundle. Windows: C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3. Mac: ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3. Linux: ~/.vst3. Rescan VST3 plugins in your DAW.

Linux requires x86-64, glibc 2.34+ and the X11/XCB, Cairo and Pango runtime libraries documented in INSTALL.md. Linux passed 47 VST3 validator tests plus UI controls, six page renders and active-DSP smoke checks. Compatibility with every DAW/distribution is not claimed. Mac is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. No AU build.

Force / MPC: choose the mpc-armv7 ZIP or install through OpenPlugin on compatible OS 3.x community hosts. Save before running the device installer: it restarts the music application. Gen2/aarch64 is not included.

versions.notes:
Dig for records by genre, style, decade and country on Discogs, then stream and play them into your MPC track. Needs a network connection.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Crate-Digger-1.1.8 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Crate-Digger-1.1.8/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/sd88me - VST - Crate Digger/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **Crate Digger** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

versions.notes:
Drum machine voice set ported from athousanddetails' schwung-CW-78, as an MPC/Force VST2 instrument.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r CW-78-1.2.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/CW-78-1.2.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/athousanddetails - VST - CW-78/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **CW-78** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

versions.notes:
**Daemon 1.0.0: your AI generative assistant for the Akai MPC and Force.**

![Daemon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-daemon/main/docs/screenshots/daemon.png)

### Downloads
| Device | Files | MPC OS |
|---|---|---|
| Force and first-generation MPCs (Gen 1, armv7) | `Daemon-1.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip` + `Daemon-Listen-1.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip` | 2.x and 3.x |
| Second-generation MPCs (Gen 2, aarch64) | `Daemon-1.0.0-mpc-aarch64.zip` + `Daemon-Listen-1.0.0-mpc-aarch64.zip` | 3.x |

Each zip has an `INSTALL.md` and an `install.sh`. Daemon Listen is the voice-input effect (optional).

### What it does
- Makes chords, melodies, basslines and beats from a sentence, typed or spoken, in your key, scale and length, playing in time with MPC.
- Agent mode (CONTROL MPC) builds the session around them: adds tracks, loads instruments, presets and effects, sets synth parameters and
  puts parts into clips, always as a plan you read before pressing RUN.
- Gemini (Google) or Claude (Anthropic), chosen on the SETTINGS tab. Voice input uses Gemini.

### Tested
Verified on an Akai Force with MPC OS 3.9.1. Gen 2 hardware and MPC OS 2.x are supported by the build (glibc 2.28 for armv7, the
2.x skin format) but not yet tested on a device. Agent mode's screen automations ship for the Force on MPC OS 3.9.1.

## What is new

- **MPC OS 2.x**: the touchscreen skin is in the 2.x shape. On MPC OS 2.x the pages should now draw; with 1.0.5 and earlier they stayed empty (the plugin still played from the Q-Links).
- Everything from 1.0.5 is included: the BANKS page Q-Links (bank, patch, page back and forward), one cart per Q-Link turn or wheel click, lists that read top to bottom, and three Q-Link events per option on the key-scaling curves.
- Same library (glibc 2.29), same parameters: saved projects load as before, and your own `.syx` carts are kept on upgrade.

## What was tried (please read)

The "MPC OS 2.x + 3.x" label is a check of the skin and library against MPC OS 2.15.1's own skins, **not a test of this release on a 2.x unit**. This exact skin (the 2.x shape with the new BANKS page) had not been run on a device when it was released. What was tried: the 2.x shape with 1.0.4's pages worked on a Force and, per a tester, on a 2.15.1 MPC Live; 1.0.5's BANKS page worked on a Force in the 3.x shape. If a page misbehaves on your device, **1.0.5 is the fallback** (MPC OS 3.x only), and a report is welcome.

**CPU** (Force, `tools/bench.sh`, 2026-10-05, same library as 1.0.5): worst block 5.4% of the audio budget, worst p99 4.0%, 1.7% mean at 16 voices (PASS).

## Requirements

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Dexed-DX7-1.0.6 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/sd88me - VST - Dexed (DX7)/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Your own files go in `dx7_carts/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/sd88me - VST - Dexed (DX7)/`); the installer keeps them when you upgrade and uninstall, and moves them there from the old `/sdcard/vst` location if you had installed the plugin that way.

and the Q-Links follow the page.

plugins.name: Drips
plugins.author: Padbangers
plugins.summary: Drips: a granular texture synthesizer with four recording qualities, a delay and beat slicer, tempo-synced seeding, wavetables and a modulation page, from Émilie Gillet's open-source Beads.

manifest.name: Drips
manifest.about: Granular texture synthesizer built on Emilie Gillet's open-source Beads DSP: four recording qualities, delay and beat slicer, tempo-synced Seed, wavetable mode and a modulation page.

versions.notes:
**Drips 1.0.0** — a granular texture synthesizer for Akai MPC standalone devices, as an insert effect, built on Émilie Gillet's open-source Beads DSP.

- Records the track into a 4–32 s buffer and replays it as up to 30 grains; four recording qualities (Bright Digital, Cold Digital, Sunny Tape, Scorched Cassette), each at its own sample rate.
- Delay and beat slicer (SIZE fully clockwise), tempo-synced to the MPC.
- Seed latched, gated, or clocked by MIDI notes or the MPC tempo; optional MIDI split (channel 1 pitch, channel 2 seed).
- Wavetable mode (no input needed), two envelopes, two LFOs and an 8-slot modulation matrix, a built-in manual.

Tested on an **Akai MPC X** (MPC OS 3.9.1). CPU on the MPC X: p99 9.9 %, worst block 11.1 % — PASS. MPC OS 3.x.

SHA-256 of `Drips-1.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip`: `4362a35b664c369ffbca05650518b190227252a9671625e980c6ae9fc1656b5b`

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61). The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Drips-1.0.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Drips-1.0.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies the plugin folder into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place.

Then add **Drips** to a track from the plugin browser (Insert effects, Padbangers). Full instructions, manual install and uninstall: `INSTALL.md` in the zip.

versions.notes:
**Fixed: Euclidier stopped after a few minutes and needed a reload.** The background engine was crashing (SIGSEGV). Its MIDI-clock filter grew the input thread's stack each time MPC's clock and Euclidier's own clock alternated, and it never freed the clock events it rejected. Found and fixed by @SamplingHigh (with Codex), who ran the fixed engine on a Force (MPC OS 3.9.1) with no restarts and no lost MIDI output. Thank you!

Also guarded two edge cases: a tempo estimate before the first clock pulses arrive, and the random-CC velocity when both values are equal.

**Tested:** on a Force (MPC OS 3.9.1), running for over 15 minutes with the transport going: one engine process, no restarts, no exit or signal in the log, stack steady at 132 KB. Offline: grid test and armhf build pass. The CPU benchmark was not re-run for this build.

**Requirements and install:** as 1.0.7. Unzip, copy the folder to the device, run `install.sh` (it stops and restarts MPC). Running it again upgrades in place. MPC OS 2.x + 3.x (glibc 2.30), first-generation devices (Force, Live, One, X, Key).

If it still drops out, please send `/tmp/euclidier_vst.log` (over SSH, before restarting MPC).

# Euclidier 1.0.1

Fixes for 1.0.0. If you installed 1.0.0, install this over it (the installer upgrades in place).

**Fixed**
- **Tempo too fast.** MPC sends its own MIDI clock to every MIDI port (a device's *sync* setting), on top of the clock the plugin makes from the project transport, so the engine ran too fast. It now follows only the plugin's clock, whatever the port's sync setting is.
- **MIDI port name.** The port showed as "Mockba Euclidier"; it is now "Euclidier". You may need to enable the new "Euclidier" device for your tracks in Preferences, MIDI (the old "Mockba Euclidier" entry can be ignored).
- A second Euclidier instance gets its own port ("Euclidier 2", ...), and a removed and re-inserted instance gets the same name back, so MPC keeps its settings.

An 8-lane Euclidean MIDI sequencer as a native plugin for Akai MPC OS standalone devices (Force, MPC Live / One / X / Key). It plays no sound: it sends MIDI to other tracks from its own "Euclidier" MIDI port.

**What's in it**
- **LANES** tab: edit one lane. A pattern circle with a play-head, knobs for steps, fill, shift, loop, gate, velocity, humanise, note and MIDI channel, a division stepper, NOTE / DRUM and enable.
- **ALL** tab: all 8 lanes as live pattern rows with a play-head, an enable lamp and a RANDOMISE button per lane.
- **RANDOMISE ALL** and **DRUM MODE ALL** in the top bar. A new instance starts with every lane in drum mode, lanes 1-4 on, each with its own pattern.
- Up to 32 steps per lane. The engine is bundled in the plugin folder.
- CPU on a Force: worst p99 2.0% of the audio block (PASS).

After installing, enable the "Euclidier" MIDI port for the tracks that should receive it in Preferences, MIDI.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Euclidier-1.0.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Euclidier-1.0.1/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/sd88me - VST - Euclidier/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **Euclidier** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

versions.notes:
# Changelog

## 0.2.0

Tested on an Akai Force (MPC OS 3.9.1).

- PET: a second grain engine, CLOUDS (Mutable Instruments Clouds with the Parasites firmware: granular, stretch,
  looping delay, spectral, Oliverb, Resonestor) beside XXL GRAINS (ENGINE). The knobs show what they do in each mode.
  SCALE snaps PITCH (and CLOUD's scattered grains) to a scale; GRAIN SYNC puts grains on the beat grid.
- TAPE: loops up to 3 minutes; SEND (the loop goes through PET / FX / SPACE / GATE, or plays clean); REC OUT (record
  what you hear instead of the input); overdub the radio on top of a playing loop; UNDO / REDO per layer.
- SAVE / AUTO SAVE: the loop as eviltunerrec01.wav, 02 ... (24-bit) in "Force Documents/Evil Tuner XXL Recordings";
  AUTO SAVE writes every recording and overdub to a new file.
- AIRPLAY: Apple devices listed the receiver but could not connect (the Apple-Response was wrong with mbedTLS 3);
  fixed, and the receiver advertises its own host name and only the address of the network it is on.
- Larger text everywhere; knob names are live.
- The mpc-vst-plugins wrapper's Q-Link / automation UpdateDisplay fix (#486-#489).

## 0.1.1
- Packed under **L'Cronx**: the plugin folder is now `L'Cronx - VST - Evil Tuner XXL` and MPC lists the maker as L'Cronx. Nothing else
  changed from 0.1.0. If you installed 0.1.0, run its `uninstall.sh` first (copy out anything you saved inside the plugin
  folder), then install 0.1.1. The installer handles the ' in the folder name.

## 0.1.0

First release (offline-tested).

- Sources: RADIO (Radio Browser: browse by genre, country, sort and bitrate, search with an on-screen keyboard,
  favourites, SYNC to start with MPC's Play, ICY titles, auto-reconnect), PHONE (Roc / Roc Droid receiver on udp
  10001-10003) and AIRPLAY (classic AirPlay, shows the title), each a static helper program.
- PET: 8-voice granular engine on the last 8 s (position, size, pitch, grains, spread, cloud, detune, shape, freeze,
  KEYS), LP / HP / BP / COMB / DUAL filter with an envelope, oscillator layer, RANDOM.
- FX: Loop Saboteur's eleven output stages, an eight-mode saturator, a look-ahead limiter.
- SPACE: the Erica-style delay from LXRXXL BAZZLINE; Dragonfly Plate, reverse and Room reverb with shimmer.
- GATE: 16-step trance gate with patterns and swing, stutter, MIDI duck.
- TAPE: a rolling 3-minute tape, a tempo-synced looper (capture, overdub, reverse, half / double, undo, to grains) and
  background STRETCH renders (Paulstretch, freeze, stutter, cloud, half tape, reverse).
- MOD: three LFOs (free or synced), an envelope follower, the keys' ADSR.
- Seven pages: a classic tuner RADIO page and six modern effect pages.

## Force Link Audio 1.1.0 — OpenMPC add-in

Publish the Force's stereo main mix as a Link Audio channel while keeping the
Force standalone. By Mac Digi / Rare Data, originally built for the COMPA project.

This release adds the OpenMPC catalog package and shared installer. The audio tap
stays small; the Link Audio publisher remains a separate process and now exits
when its MPC parent exits. The build targets armhf/glibc 2.31; other MPC hardware
is unverified.

**Network audio is off by default.** Read README-addin.txt, disable the old
MockbaMod ForceLinkAudio addon if present, then install the new package. Set
`enabled=1` in the installed settings only when you want to publish audio on your
trusted LAN. Save your project before the installer restarts MPC.

Original legacy releases remain available. This package uses the unmodified
OpenMPC shared installer and preserves other preload entries. See INSTALL.md for
its changes and uninstall procedure, including the shared boot-reload integration.

Source: the matching tag in this repository. GPL-2.0-or-later; third-party notices
are included. Thanks to sd88me/OpenMPC, MockbaMod contributors and Amit Talwar.

### Verification

Catalog validation, 12 config-parser cases, 77 shared-installer checks and the
isolated ARM lifecycle test passed. Real Force installation, settings preservation and rollback passed. The owner
confirmed normal local sound and controls while looping a saved project. A Mac
Link Audio receiver captured 641,000 non-silent stereo frames with no clipping.
Other MPC models remain unverified.

versions.notes:
Sampled guitars (acoustic archtop, electric), harps, strumstick, violin, dan tranh and psaltery on a six-string playing model, with a synth layer, chord pads, drive, chorus, echo and space. All samples CC0.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Fretty-0.8.5 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Fretty-0.8.5/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/3dthc - VST - Fretty/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **Fretty** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

manifest.name: GHOST
manifest.about: GHOST BOTH FIX stereo glitch effect; identical approved audio binary.
manifest.requires: Gen1 MPC with root shell access, BusyBox and systemctl. Device-side transactional installer.

versions.notes:
# GHOST 2.4.2 — installer2-rc3 Community Beta

Installer-only prerelease. The GHOST 2.4.2 BOTH FIX DSP, GUI, UID, parameter indices, Q-Links and presets are unchanged. The original v2.4.2 release/tag/assets are preserved.

**Tested ZIP SHA-256:** `0920fde1c908e9a3dcdde5182dffeb206b63b8e706e16c7fb46839a9b0be0b7e`  
**Unchanged audio binary:** `588019130b31ced7077f7e4afe35bd23b0753df7a2959e2af39fa825e1b81afd`

## Installer corrections

Post-stop stable settings boundary; serialized worker/watchdog rollback; explicit recovery/work roots outside plugin discovery; boot/PID/start-time lock ownership; strict numeric XML entity decoding; pinned legacy desktop metadata adoption. Runtime conflicts refuse; presets and unknown user files are preserved. No broad cleanup of Synths.

## Verified scope

- 84 offline tests; ShellCheck passes. Catalog ZIP validation: zero errors, two custom-installer warnings requiring maintainer review.
- Actual MPC One Gen1 / Hakai 3.9.1: install, legacy-format-to-community-format migration update, uninstall and preferred-installation restore all returned 0 with integrity checks.
- Owner confirmed GUI/navigation, touch, Q-Links, audio/MIX and basic stability after install and after restore. Not exhaustive parameter or endurance testing.
- 52 FXP and 82 foreign registrations/plugin binary hashes preserved; final original 366 files and settings bytes restored exactly. No unexpected restart/crash observed.
- The migration update keeps audio/product version 2.4.2. No semantic-version upgrade or catalog-client notification coverage is claimed. Shutdown-rewrite/race/stale-lock faults were tested offline, not physically injected.

## Install and recovery

Read the included INSTALL.md before running install.sh. Use root shell, actual writable executable Synths path and explicit validated recovery/work roots outside ALL content discovery locations. Work must share the target filesystem. Example roots on the tested device were /storage/GHOST-Recovery and /storage/GHOST-Work; do not assume they are correct for every device. Save project changes first. The host screen may go black during intended stop/start. Keep each transaction's verified backup and recovery context.

Use the documented community -y/-n/-t contract. With -n, the batch caller owns host lifecycle. Uninstall removes recognized GHOST runtime/registration and retains presets/unknown user files. Recovery capacity is bounded by refusal; completed recovery points are not deleted automatically. No physical power-loss/storage-failure test or Gen2/OS2.x compatibility claim.

## Downloads

- Installation ZIP and SHA256SUMS below.
- [Hardware terminal logs and owner confirmations](https://github.com/carballocba/MPC-EURO-/tree/v2.4.2-installer2-rc3/evidence/hardware-rc3); private settings/backups excluded.
- [Consolidated hardware report](https://github.com/carballocba/MPC-EURO-/blob/v2.4.2-installer2-rc3/GHOST_HARDWARE_TEST_RESULTS.md).
- [Corresponding committed source, installer and tests](https://github.com/carballocba/MPC-EURO-/tree/v2.4.2-installer2-rc3); use GitHub source downloads for this tag.
- [Existing five-page User Manual](https://github.com/carballocba/MPC-EURO-/releases/download/v2.4.2/GHOST_2.4.2_User_Manual.pdf) and [Quick Start](https://github.com/carballocba/MPC-EURO-/releases/download/v2.4.2/GHOST_QUICK_START.md). These unchanged audio/control manuals apply; use this package's INSTALL.md for installation.

The original desktop recovery package remains available on v2.4.2. GPL-3.0-only with retained third-party notices. Catalog PR571 remains subject to sd88me's review; this prerelease is not catalog approval.

versions.notes:
A random sampler after Mutable Instruments Marbles (random gates, melodies and deja vu loops) that plays other tracks over MIDI or analog gear over the MPC X's CV jacks, with two envelopes, two LFOs and a modulation matrix.

**SHA-256** `Glass-Spheres-1.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip`: `c09d22a5347e4c9324c9e8bf3ace1fb79f56a237fc851554a3040e536effff9c`

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61, Force). The installer refuses anything else. CV output needs an MPC X.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on an **MPC X with MPC OS 3.9.1**. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device: `scp -r Glass-Spheres-1.0.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Save your project, then run: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Glass-Spheres-1.0.0/install.sh`

The installer copies the plugin folder to `/sdcard/Synths`, stops MPC, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds Glass Spheres to the plugin list and starts MPC again. Then add **Glass Spheres** from *Instrument plugins* on a track of its own.

Uninstall: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Glass-Spheres-1.0.0/uninstall.sh`

## CPU

Measured on the MPC X with the framework's `tools/bench.sh`: worst p99 **3.8%** of one audio block, worst block 6.6%, verdict **PASS**.

## Notes

- **MIDI:** every instance opens its own MIDI port, **Glass Spheres 1**, **Glass Spheres 2**, ... On the track to be played, pick it as the MIDI input with the voice's channel and turn monitoring on. Three voices (gate T1-T3, pitch X1-X3 / Y / fixed note, channel each) and two CC lanes on the OUTPUT tab.
- **CV (MPC X):** each of the seven outputs to any of CV 1-8, 0-5 V at 1 V/octave. Don't use the same jacks on CV tracks.
- Clock: internal, MPC tempo and transport, or MIDI notes on its own track.

plugins.name: InterzoneXXL
plugins.author: L'Cronx
plugins.summary: Valley Audio's Interzone synth voice from VCV Rack, played from MIDI in mono or up to 16-voice poly on the module's own panel. Every input jack is patched to a built-in source (LFOs, sequencers, random) on the MPC tempo, with a brickwall limiter and 16 presets.

manifest.name: InterzoneXXL
manifest.about: InterzoneXXL by L'Cronx: Valley Audio's Interzone synth voice for MPC OS

versions.notes:
> **0.1.3** is 0.1.2 built on the latest wrapper and includes the Q-Link and automation fix (#486–#489): Q-Links now move parameters on the track's automation screen. Nothing else changed. Installs over 0.1.2 in place.

**InterzoneXXL — Valley Audio's Interzone synth voice, played from MIDI in mono or poly and patched with its own LFOs, random sources and sequencers, running natively inside MPC OS on the Akai Force.**

Load it as a plugin instrument on a track: a VCO with glide, pitch mod, PWM and a sub wave, a mixer with noise, a resonant 2/4-pole OTA filter with a high-pass, an LFO with seven waves, a looping envelope and a VCA, on pages drawn from the module's own panel, sliders and switches. Every input jack picks a source running inside the plugin: four Bogaudio LFOs, Tidal Modulator 2, Random Sampler, two CV and two gate sequencers on the MPC tempo, an extra oscillator, Interzone's own outputs, velocity, mod wheel and pressure.

> ✅ **0.1.1 is tested on an Akai Force** (MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod). Offline, the plugin's output is also checked against Valley's own Interzone module code, sample for sample (patched cables included), under ASan + UBSan. Save your projects before installing, and report problems under **Issues**. Full list: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sunskiefer/InterzoneXXL/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Pages
**VCO** · **FILTER / LFO** · **MIXER / ENV** · **VOICE** (voice, limiter, Panic · EXT OSC · PRESETS) · **CV IN** · **LFO** (1-4) · **TIDAL / RANDOM** · **SEQ** (Seq 1-2, Gate 1-2, SEQ SET)

## Requirements
- Akai Force (first generation); other Gen1 MPC OS units should work but are untested
- MPC OS 3.x
- Root SSH access (for example MockbaMod)

## Install
Download **InterzoneXXL-0.1.1-mpc-armv7.zip** below, unzip it, then:

    scp -r InterzoneXXL-0.1.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/
    ssh -t root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/InterzoneXXL-0.1.1/install.sh

The installer stops MPC (save first), installs the plugin, and starts MPC again. Then load **InterzoneXXL** (manufacturer L'Cronx) as a plugin instrument. Presets go in `/sdcard/InterzoneXXL Presets`.

Guide: [docs/USER_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/sunskiefer/InterzoneXXL/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md)

## Credits
- **Interzone:** Dale Johnson (Valley Audio)
- **LFO:** Matt Demanett (Bogaudio) · **Tidal Modulator 2 and Random Sampler:** Emilie Gillet (Mutable Instruments Tides 2 and Marbles), VCV's port in Audible Instruments
- **Patching, sources, presets, limiter, Panic:** from [PlateauXXL](https://github.com/sunskiefer/PlateauXXL) and [RMXXXL](https://github.com/sunskiefer/RMXXXL)
- **Plugin framework, skin tools and installer:** sd88me ([mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins))
- **Artwork:** Valley (ValleyRackFree), VCV Component Library (CC BY-NC 4.0), Bogaudio (CC BY-SA 4.0) · **Interface font:** Titillium Web (SIL Open Font License)

Six-voice Juno-style polysynth (ultramaster_kr106 DSP) with 256 factory presets and a realistic panel skin. Tested on a Force (MPC OS 3.9.1); the aarch64 zip (Gen2) is untested.

CPU on a Force: six held notes about 31% of a block at 2x oversampling (20% at 1x); a fast Q-Link sweep peaks at 47% at p99 (bench verdict FAIL). Use 1x oversampling (SETTINGS) and one instance on a busy project.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r JN-106-0.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/JN-106-0.1.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/sd88me - VST - JN-106/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **JN-106** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

## Install by hand

1. Copy `portable/sd88me - VST - JN-106/` to `/sdcard/Synths/sd88me - VST - JN-106/`. It holds `kr106.so`, `plugin-meta.xml`, `version.xml`, `Plugin Skins/`
   and the data:
2. Stop MPC: `systemctl stop acvs`. If there is no `acvs` service (`systemctl cat acvs` fails, as on some MPC OS 2.x versions and on Hakai-enabled systems), use `systemctl stop inmusic-mpc`.
3. Back up the settings file, `MPC.settings` (on a Force: `/media/az01-internal/Settings/MPC/MPC.settings`).
4. In `MPC.settings`, inside `<VALUE name="pluginList-arm"><KNOWNPLUGINS>`, add the line from `plugin-meta.xml` with
   `%payload-path%` replaced by `/sdcard/Synths`. If there is no `pluginList-arm` value yet, add one just before `</PROPERTIES>`:
   ```xml
   <VALUE name="pluginList-arm">
     <KNOWNPLUGINS>
       (the line from plugin-meta.xml)
     </KNOWNPLUGINS>
   </VALUE>
   ```
5. Start MPC: `systemctl start acvs`, or `systemctl start inmusic-mpc` if that is the service you stopped. If MPC shows default settings, restore your backup (the XML was malformed).

Edit `MPC.settings` only while MPC is stopped: MPC can save its own copy over a change made while it runs. Tools that
rebuild the whole plugin list from the plugin folders in `Synths` keep this plugin, because it is such a folder.

versions.notes:
# Liminal Amp 1.0.2

Gen 1 gets the same fast cab as Gen 2.

## Changes
- **Faster cab IR on Gen 1.** The Force / MPC Live / Live II / One / X / Key 61 build now runs the cabinet IR's FFT with
  NEON, as the Gen 2 build already did. Until now the Gen 1 build used slower plain (scalar) code for it. The sound
  doesn't change: the IR is still processed to the official NAM plugin's spec (up to 8192 samples, its resampling and
  level), checked against the official convolution on 32-bit ARM. The cab uses less CPU, which leaves more room for
  other plugins or for **A2 Full**.

Both builds now run the same code the same way: same sound, same options (Eco, A2 Full, IR length), same presets.
Gen 2 hardware is simply faster.

Nothing else changes. Projects and presets from 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 open as they were.

## Install
On a Gen 1 device use one of these two zips: **`Liminal-Amp-for-MPC-OS-1.0.2.zip`** (copy the `Gm0rb - VST - Liminal Amp`
folder into `Synths` and run `vstscanner.sh`) or **`Liminal-Amp-1.0.2-mpc-armv7.zip`** (MPC OS Plugin Catalog, with
`install.sh`). On a Gen 2 device use **`Liminal-Amp-1.0.2-mpc-aarch64.zip`** with its `install.sh`, or the catalog
(tested under emulation only so far:
[docs/GEN2.md](https://github.com/gmorb/mpc-vst-liminal-amp/blob/main/docs/GEN2.md)).
Your `models`, `irs` and `presets` folders are kept.

Requires MPC OS 3.x on a Gen 1 Force / MPC, or a Gen 2 MPC (the aarch64 zip).

A small update to [1.0.0](../v1.0.0): smoother taps, and a measured CPU figure for the MPC OS Plugin Catalog.

versions.notes:
- New page (v3), in the design system of the companion plugin Liminal Hz (one page, near-black textured background,
  large type, engraved knobs, one accent that means "a live value") with this plugin's own identity: a guitar amp.
  Warm valve glow in the lower right, faint drifting air across the page, amber knob arcs. Same controls, bigger text.
- AMP LIST and CAB LIST: tap-to-load lists (four 44 px rows to a page, "pack . name", PREV / NEXT / CLOSE, the one in use
  marked), opened over their block, as Liminal Hz's IR LIST. Long names slide. Parameters 36-59 (appended; state files
  and automation do not include them).
- Fast start: the folders found last time are kept in a hidden index (`.models-index`, `.irs-index`) in the plugin
  folder. A project's saved amp and cab load from it as soon as the plugin opens, before the full search of the drives
  finishes; the search then refreshes the lists. (Liminal Hz's library code.)
- My Presets (as Liminal Hz): the header shows the preset in use ("My: <name>") beside **MY PRESETS**, which opens a
  list over the AMP block (three to a page, PREV / NEXT / CLOSE). **SAVE** keeps the current sound (every setting, the
  amp and the cab) named after its amp ("Plexi Crunch", "Plexi Crunch 2"...); tap a row to load it (the amp and cab are
  found again even if a card moved; a missing one is named); **DELETE** asks twice. A project remembers the selected
  preset. Presets are `presets/<name>.na2p` text files, kept across upgrades, renamable from a computer (RESCAN).
  Parameters 75-79 (appended; not saved in projects, not automatable); amp_menu gained a third option (Presets).
- The phone pages in the Liminal Amp look (warm black, the valves' amber glow, faceplate cards, the Liminal Amp wordmark,
  Titillium Web shipped in `art/fonts` with its OFL licence, 48 px buttons). The home page offers TONE3000 and
  **My Presets**. **NAME ON PHONE** opens `<address>/presets` (no internet or libcurl needed): save the current sound
  under a typed name, load, rename, delete, and **edit** a preset: its amp and cab (from the plugin's lists) and every
  setting, grouped as on the MPC (input, tone, out, cab, amp), then Save or Save and load.
- The amp's pluck print: under the amp's name, one plucked A string played through the loaded capture, drawn as a
  waveform (14 slices; parameters 61-74, read-only, not saved, not automatable). A clean amp shows a sharp attack that
  fades; crunch holds the note and evens its peaks; high gain is a solid wall. Measured when a capture loads, in the
  background (the capture alone, at its own rate, 1.2 s of audio), then the capture is reset before it plays. The amp's
  detail ("Amp · NAM · @creator", "Model 2 of 4 · Local") moved to the right of its pack line.
- Glowing valves (lower right): three KT88 power valves (glass, silvered getter, wide ribbed anode with two slots, mica,
  heater loops) on a chassis lip show the amp's output level (parameter 60 `tubes`, read-only, 25 states): heaters glow
  dull red in silence and heat up one after another as you play, cooling over about 2.5 s. Not saved, not automatable;
  one peak scan per audio block.
- A2 FULL switch (off by default): plays an A2 capture at its Full size (8 channels) instead of Lite (3 channels),
  reloaded in the background; the detail line then ends in "· Full". On a Gen 1 Force the Full size alone takes
  about 57% of an audio block (Lite about 12%): for simple projects, or faster hardware.
- A2 FULL takes two taps: the first shows a warning ("A2 FULL: very heavy on CPU", "Best on a G2. Own risk.", "Tap A2 FULL again to turn on") and stays
  off; a second tap within six seconds turns it on. Off is one tap. A project or preset saved with it on loads it as saved.
- The phone page uses this plugin's own port (8091) and, when that's taken (another instance), the next free one;
  a page that closed itself after 15 idle minutes opens again on the next press (it used to stay closed).
- Brand: "Liminal Amp" by the manufacturer "Gm0rb" (folder `Gm0rb - VST - Liminal Amp`, `liminal_amp.so`, catalog id
  `liminal-amp`). Renamed before release from "NAM A2", then "Liminal Stack", which MPC's insert slot showed as "Limin.l Stack"
  (also without the space). The internal plugin uid (`NmA2`) and the project and preset formats are unchanged.
- README images (`docs/images/`: banner, page, signal chain, controls, lists, My Presets, pluck print and valves, A2 FULL,
  the phone pages), made by `tools/make_readme_images.py` from the running plugin and its real web server
  (`tools/readme_demo.cpp` drives the host build).
- Header: the preset readout no longer overprints the wordmark (wordmark slightly smaller; the preset, MY PRESETS, TONE3000
  logo and status line moved right; the status line is narrower). Before first use the TONE3000 line says "Tap BROWSE TONE3000".
- The A2 FULL switch's parameter is named "A2 Full" (was "Full", which MPC showed next to the cab's FULL / SHORT). Only the
  shown name changed: projects and presets keep it by key. tools/honest_preview.py now draws a control's name as MPC does (the
  parameter's name, and knob values in upper case), so the README images match the device.
- DELETE (in each block's header): deletes a capture or a cab IR permanently, in two taps (the first asks: "Tap DELETE again to
  delete it permanently", for 4 s). When the last file of a downloaded TONE3000 pack goes, its tone3000.json and
  folder go too. Only .nam / .wav files inside the scanned folders can be deleted.
- Cab IRs: our own WAV reader (engine/wav_reader) instead of AudioDSPTools' loader. It reads the files IR
  libraries ship that the official loader refuses: WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE without a `fact` chunk (written by many
  DAWs; the official loader calls them "invalid"), 64-bit float, and stereo (averaged to mono; the chain is mono).
  Identical samples to the official loader wherever it reads a file, except 32-bit integer PCM, which it loads with
  inverted polarity (a `1 << 31` overflow); here the polarity is correct.
- CAB's BROWSE TONE3000 shows cabinet IRs only (gears=cab): reverb "Spaces" IRs need far longer convolution than
  a cab section (they're for the separate Liminal Hz plugin).
- New page (one page, dark): AMP and CAB blocks, each with the tone pack (TONE3000 tone or folder), the model
  name in large type, a detail line (TONE3000: gear type, format and @creator; local: "Model 2 of 4"), PREV/NEXT
  PACK, and BROWSE TONE3000; the T3K mark on a block whose tone came from TONE3000; the full TONE3000 logo with the
  status line; all controls in one row. Laid out to TONE3000's design requirements (entry point at the block,
  partnership splash, loaded-tone attribution, logo before mark); tone images aren't possible on an MPC page.
- ECO switch (off by default): runs the capture at MPC's 44.1 kHz without resampling, for lower CPU; the
  capture's tone then shifts slightly (about 8% lower in frequency). Switching is faded to avoid a click.
- NeuralAmpModelerCore v0.5.4 (was v0.5.2): A2 captures as TONE3000 serves them now take NAM's A2 fast path.
  v0.5.2 required head_scale == 0.01, which trained captures don't have, and ran them on the generic path at
  about 3x the CPU (a real capture measured 34% on a Force for the model alone). The fast path's output matches
  the generic path's within float rounding; tools/a2_shape_test guards it.
- First release: a lightweight, official-sound Neural Amp Modeler for Gen 1 Akai Force / MPC. A2 captures at
  their Lite size with the official NAM plugin's signal chain (noise gate, tone stack, cabinet IR, normalized
  output), resampled 44.1 <-> 48 kHz around the model as the official plugin does.
- Browses .nam models and .wav cabinet IRs in any `models` and `irs` folders on the device's drives (and in the
  plugin's own folder), with subfolders as categories; loads in the background, so browsing never cuts the sound.
- GET TONES: pick A2 captures or cab IRs on TONE3000 from a phone on the same Wi-Fi (TONE3000's Select flow); they
  download into the plugin's models/ and irs/ folders with a credit file, and load. Uses the device's libcurl; no
  account data is stored on the device.
- Projects keep the model and IR by name: found again when a card or folder changes.
- Cabinet IRs by FFT convolution (identical to the official plugin's, far cheaper); optional Short IR length.
- Measured on a Force (RK3288): the whole chain with an 8192-sample IR uses ~16% of an audio block (p99 ~19%).

os_compat_why: needs glibc 2.34, MPC OS 2.x has about 2.32
versions.notes:
### New
- **LONG IR** (Gen 1): a button under Reverse that brings Gen 2's IR quality to the Force and Gen 1 MPCs: IRs up to
  **20 s** instead of 5 (so Decay 300% on a 5 s room rings its full ~15 s), band-limited sinc resampling for IRs at other
  sample rates and for Stretch (no dulled top octave, no alias tones), and Decay analysed at twice the frequency detail.
  It is CPU heavy, so it takes two taps: the first only warns ("CPU heavy · tap again"), a second within 4 s turns it on;
  one tap turns it off. It's a device setting: a project remembers it, presets and Init leave it alone, and it is never
  automation. On Gen 2 it reads "Gen 2 · always on".

### Changed
- **Gen 1 is cheaper to run, with LONG IR off too:**
  - the third ("far") convolution stage, until now Gen 2 only, is on in both builds. Past 0.74 s an IR runs in
    16384-sample blocks on its own worker, so a 5 s IR needs about a quarter of the partitions it did;
  - the FFT runs PFFFT's NEON code. Until now the Gen 1 build ran PFFFT's scalar code, because the build flag that
    enables NEON was never set.
  Both give the same result as before (equal to direct convolution, `tools/bench_reverb --check`); only the CPU cost drops.
  On a PC (`tools/bench_reverb`, real time, 5 s stereo IR) the worker's load falls from 1.9% to 0.7% of a core, and a
  20 s IR with LONG IR on costs 1.3%: less than a 5 s IR did in 1.2.0. The audio thread's cost is unchanged. Not yet
  measured on a Force (docs/HANDOFF.md lists what to measure).
- **Faster re-preparation:** the resampled IR is kept, so turning Start, End, the fades, Decay or Reverse no longer
  resamples the file again (only a new file, Stretch or LONG IR do). With LONG IR on, a 20 s 48 kHz IR re-prepares after
  End, a fade or Reverse in about 0.12 s instead of about 1 s on a PC.
- `engine/platform.h`: the IR quality (`Quality`: length cap, sinc, Decay FFT) is now a runtime setting instead of
  build constants; `LIMINAL_GEN2` makes the high quality the only one.
- Tests: the high-quality tests run in both builds; `ARM=1` now also runs the convolution check and the engine tests
  as armv7 programs (NEON) under qemu-arm; plugin tests for LONG IR's two taps, its time-out, projects, Init and presets.

versions.notes:
### New
- **Gen 2 build (MPC Live III and other RK3588 units, 64-bit).** The release now carries a second zip,
  `Liminal-Hz-<version>-mpc-aarch64.zip`, next to the Gen 1 one: the same plugin (same id, uid, parameters, presets
  and page), so a project moves between generations. Its installer registers it under `pluginList-arm-64bit`.
- **Gen 2 lifts the Gen 1 limits** (engine/platform.h), since the RK3588 has far more headroom than the Force's RK3288:
  - **IRs up to 20 s** (Gen 1: 5 s). Long halls, drones and long echo IRs play whole.
  - **Decay reaches its full length**: 300% on a 5 s room now rings to about 15 s; on Gen 1 it stopped at the 5 s cap.
  - **A third convolution stage** for long IRs: taps past 0.74 s run in 16384-sample blocks on their own worker
    thread, so a 20 s stereo IR costs the audio thread exactly what a 5 s one does (the same 93 ms zero-latency head),
    and the background work is a fraction of what 2048-sample blocks would need. Still zero latency, still equal to
    direct convolution (`tools/bench_reverb --check`: about 133 dB below the signal).
  - **Band-limited IR resampling** (Kaiser-windowed sinc, 64 zero crossings) instead of cubic interpolation, for IRs
    at other sample rates and for **Stretch**. A 48 kHz IR keeps its top octave (cubic lost 1.9 dB at 17 kHz) and
    Stretch below 100% no longer folds high partials back down as alias tones (cubic: a full-level alias; now -77 dB).
  - **Finer Decay analysis**: an STFT of 4096 (10.8 Hz bins) instead of 2048, so the bass third-octave bands are
    measured and continued from real resolution; same 11.6 ms time step.
  - **NEON FFT** (PFFFT's NEON path; the Gen 1 build has always used PFFFT's scalar code).
- Tested on an MPC Live III (Gen 2) and an Akai Force (Gen 1), both on MPC OS 3.9.1.
- Tests: `GEN2=1 tools/test.sh` (the Gen 2 limits on the PC), `AARCH64=1` (the convolution check, engine tests and the
  plugin test as aarch64 programs under qemu-aarch64, against the Gen 2 .so); new tests for the far stage, 15-20 s
  IRs, Decay past 5 s, and the resampler's top octave and aliasing.

### Changed
- `engine/long_convolver`: the tail is now a list of stages (each with its own worker). The Gen 1 build has one stage,
  as before; its tests pass unchanged.
- The aarch64 build sets FPCR's flush-to-zero while processing, as the armv7 build sets FPSCR's.

versions.notes:
# Lucky Dip 0.9.0

**A random drum-kit builder and inspiration machine for Akai MPC and Force.** It dips into your sample library, fills 16 pads at
random, plays the kit, and exports it as an MPC drum program. Lock what you like, reroll what you don't, and rediscover samples you
forgot you had.

First public release (0.9: feature complete, tested on an Akai Force; other devices untested).

## Highlights
- Scans your folders and sorts samples into 23 categories from folder and file names
- 16 pads filled at random, drum-kit style, with wildcard pads
- LOCK / REROLL / CLEAR per pad, per-pad category pools, favourites and rejects, match levels
- Four candy-coloured pages: PADS 1-8, PADS 9-16, PAD EDIT (follows the last pad you play) and SETTINGS
- Export to an MPC `.xpm`, copying the samples or linking to the originals
- Settings for the sample source, export folder, skip loops and max file size

## Requirements
First-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61), root SSH access. Tested on a Force
(MPC OS 3.9.1.x). Newer models are untested.

## Install
Unzip, copy the folder to the device (`scp -r Lucky-Dip-0.9.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`) and run
`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Lucky-Dip-0.9.0/install.sh`. It stops MPC (save your project first), installs the plugin and starts MPC
again. See the README for how to use it.

Optional: the 16-pad drum layout patch from mpc-vst-plugins (`tools/mpc_patch`, MPC OS 3.9.1.2 only).

CPU on a Force (bench): worst block 27.8%, p99 13.9% of a block with a random-parameter sweep: PASS.

plugins.name: Machinemodule (Gen2)
plugins.author: sd88me
plugins.summary: The Elektron Machinedrum UW sound engine as an instrument for Gen2 MPC devices: 16 tracks in one plugin, touchscreen skin, bank and kit lists, Q-Links. A ready-made download with nothing of Elektron's in it: you add your own OS file (and optionally your flash image) in the plugin folder. Gen2 only.

manifest.name: Machinemodule

user_files.label: Machinedrum OS and flash image
user_files.description: Machinemodule runs your own Machinedrum UW OS 1.63 file (a free download from Elektron). Your Machinedrum UW flash image (8 MB) is optional: it adds the ROM sample machines and the 16 factory kits.
user_files.hint: After adding the OS file, load Machinemodule once and restart MPC: it makes its skin from that file. With a flash image the first load takes about 2 minutes.

rules.label: Machinedrum UW flash image
rules.note: The right size for a Machinedrum UW flash image. The plugin reads it on its first load and makes the ROM samples and factory kits from it.

user_files.label: Your kits (optional)
user_files.description: Machinedrum kit dumps (.syx). Each file appears as a bank of kits.

rules.label: Kit dump
rules.note: An Elektron SysEx file. Its kits appear if it holds Machinedrum kits.

manifest.about: Machinemodule: the Elektron Machinedrum UW sound engine as an MPC OS instrument (Gen2; runs your own OS file)
manifest.requires: Your own Machinedrum UW OS 1.63 file (a free download from Elektron), put in the plugin's machinedrum/ folder; MPC restarted once after the first load (the plugin makes its skin from that file). No ROM machines or factory kits unless you also put your flash image (.bin) there

os_compat_why: needs glibc 2.36, MPC OS 2.x has about 2.32
versions.notes:
**Fix: pressing Stop twice no longer resets the voices.** MPC's plugin host sets the first parameter (T1 Machine) to its maximum and back on every Stop; if that jump got applied, track 1's SYN values and machine were reset. The engine now ignores that transient jump.

Same download as before: nothing of Elektron's inside; put your own Elektron_SPS1-1UW_OS1.63.syx in the plugin's machinedrum/ folder.

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r SYN-Macro-Osc-1.1.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`

and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

versions.notes:

Offline, the grid test replays MPC's measured position jitter over 50 loops and requires every clock pulse to go out with the block it belongs to.

**MPC OS:** 2.x + 3.x, as 1.0.5. CPU on a Force: worst p99 1.1%, PASS.

**Tested:** on a Force (MPC OS 3.x): tempo changes slow and fast, and note transpose. The offline grid test sweeps 60 tempo-change positions.

## What's new in 1.0.4

- **Steps follow MPC's song position.** The sequencer used to count the clock pulses it was sent from the start of play, so a start in the middle of a beat, a loop wrap, a locate or a single lost pulse could leave the steps shifted until the next restart. It now places its steps from the song position, so they stay on MPC's grid. Playing notes keep their length, and the reset-every-N-bars setting follows the song's bars (it also snaps at a loop wrap).
- **The first step on a start at the top now lands on the downbeat.** Before, it landed one clock pulse (about 20 ms at 128 BPM) early against the song grid, so you may notice the pattern sit a touch later than before.
- Checked on a Force (MPC OS 3.x) with the plugin loaded and playing; the timing is tested offline against the real sequencer core for all six note rates, a start mid-beat, a locate and lost pulses. plugins.author: L'Cronx
plugins.summary: Plays 4ms MetaModule-format patches (VCV Rack patches exported with the MetaModule hub) with 4ms's own open-source patch player and 215 built-in modules: every parameter on Q-Link pages, MIDI and the Force's clock into the patch, pads and keys to the hub's gate/CV inputs, patch outs 3-8 as MIDI for a CV track, and Wi-Fi patch upload from VCV Rack.

manifest.name: Meta4MPCXXL
manifest.about: Plays 4ms MetaModule (VCV Rack) patches on the Force: every parameter on Q-Links, MIDI, clock, CV out, Wi-Fi upload from VCV Rack.

versions.notes:
**Meta4MPCXXL** (instrument) and **Meta4MPCXXL FX** (effect) play 4ms MetaModule patches — VCV Rack patches exported with the MetaModule hub — on the Akai Force (MPC OS 3.x, armv7), with 4ms's own open-source patch player and 215 built-in modules.

- Every parameter on Q-Link pages of eight: knob sets first, then every module (names and values from the modules)
- MIDI from the track and the Force's tempo/transport (MIDI clock) into the patch
- MIDI To Hub Ins: pads/keys to the hub's Gate and CV inputs
- CV Out: patch outs 3-8 as MIDI on the plugin's own port, for a Force CV track
- Wi-Fi Receive: send patches straight from the MetaModule hub in VCV Rack
- 24 factory patches; your own patches from a `Meta4MPCXXL` folder on internal storage, SD or USB

**Pre-release: not yet run on a Force.** Tested offline (x86: all 24 factory patches, every page and knob, state, Wi-Fi, the wrapper's host test) and under ARM emulation. Device checklist: TESTING.md.

Install: the zip's INSTALL.md (the installer stops and restarts MPC). Each plugin is an 11.7 MB download, about 16 MB installed.

versions.notes:
# Model-72 1.0.0

A port of [CA-72](https://github.com/idlefoundry/ca-72) (Idle Foundry), the circuit-modelled 1970s monosynth, to Akai MPC OS
standalone: a native plugin with a skin drawn for the MPC's screen. Unofficial; not affiliated with Idle Foundry or Moog Music.
Free software, GPL-3.0-or-later; the source for this release is this tag.

- **QUALITY LO**: CA-72's light voice, MONO / POLY (2-10) / UNISON, ENTROPY, stereo, DRIVE, AUTO GAIN. About 1.3-2.7 % of a Force core a voice.
- **QUALITY HI**: one voice, a hybrid: the light oscillators, mixer and contours drive the circuit's own filter solved in real time. Within 0.2-0.6 dB of the full circuit model on most patches; 30-55 % of a Force core.
- 19 factory presets, a live stereo field, BASS COMP and PATCH mods. 4 tabs, each with Q-Links.

## Downloads
- `Model-72-1.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip`: Force, MPC Live / One / X / Key (**Gen1**). Tested on a Force.
- `Model-72-1.0.0-mpc-aarch64.zip`: MPC Live III and kin (**Gen2**). **Offline test only; not yet run on a Gen2 device.**

Unpack, follow `INSTALL.md` (the zip's `install.sh` copies the plugin to `Synths` and registers it, with a backup), restart MPC.
The skin needs MPC OS 3.x.

## Notes
- The bench's Q-Link sweep reports FAIL (p99 about 70 % of a block): it randomly switches QUALITY to HI, which takes 30-55 % of a core. In LO the bench holds at about 1.8 % mean, 2.2 % p99. Prefer LO for several tracks.
- HI's circuit filter is built on a thread at load (about 12 s on a Force the first time); LO plays at once.
- The catalog check flags `model72.so` for network / process / chroot symbols. They are Rust's statically linked standard library; the plugin calls none of them.
- Not ported from CA-72: LOCK, MIDI Learn, a track's audio into EXTERNAL INPUT, per-sound AUTO GAIN measurement.

plugins.author: sd88me
plugins.summary: The Elektron Monomachine's seven effect machines (thru, reverb, chorus, dynamix, ring mod, phaser, flanger) as an audio effect for Gen2 MPC devices, with a touchscreen skin and Q-Links. manifest.name: Monomodule FX
manifest.about: Monomodule FX: the Monomachine's effect machines as an MPC OS audio effect (Gen2; runs your own OS file)
manifest.requires: Your own Monomachine OS 1.32B file (a free download from Elektron), put in the plugin's monomodule/ folder; MPC restarted once after the first load (the plugin makes its skin from that file). Gen2 MPCs (aarch64) only

os_compat_why: needs glibc 2.36, MPC OS 2.x has about 2.32
versions.notes:
**Lower CPU on Gen2 (MPC Live III).** The DSP and voice threads now run on the Live III's fast cores (Cortex-A76) instead of a slow Cortex-A55 core, and below MPC's own audio threads in priority so they never take time from MPC's audio engine. Measured with 8 voices held: about 8% of a core, was 31%. Gen1 (Force, MPC Live/One/X): unchanged. Audio is bit-identical (gate passed on all 22 machines).

Same download as before: nothing of Elektron's inside; put your own Elektron_SFX6-60_OS1.32B.syx in the plugin's monomodule/ folder.

os_compat_why: needs glibc 2.36, MPC OS 2.x has about 2.32
versions.notes:
- **OS file check in the installer app.** Monomodule One declares its files, so the installer app's **Your ROMs and files** step checks your Monomachine OS 1.32B `.syx` (by its exact size and Elektron header) and saves it as `Elektron_SFX6-60_OS1.32B.syx` whatever it is called on your computer. Kit dumps go to `monomodule/dumps/` the same way. A kit dump is never taken as the OS file. Monomodule FX keeps reading One's copy.

versions.notes:
# Morpho-PE 1.0.1

Playtest fixes:
- The cutoff, resonance, distortion, volume, audio mod and feedback-level knobs are smoothed, so turning them no longer steps audibly.
- Distortion keeps the instrument's gain table and hard clip, with an output level makeup so a small turn of the knob no longer jumps in loudness.
- Output hack works on the right scale: the top settings now crush the sound instead of going near-silent (and no DC offset).
- Digital waves: formant waves 4-23 are two-peak vowels and the random waves 73-94 are sparse partial stacks, so a sweep changes character.
- PROGRAM page: one wide program stepper and one wide bank stepper (number and name) replace the stepper and display pairs.

A four-voice synthesizer for Akai MPC OS 3.x standalone devices, modelled on the DSI Poly Evolver's voice: two analog-style and two digital waveshape oscillators per voice, a stereo 2/4-pole lowpass, delay, tuned feedback, distortion, three envelopes, four LFOs, modulation slots and the 4 x 16 step sequencer, with a touchscreen skin, Q-Link pages and a bank browser. Poly Evolver / Evolver program dumps load as they are.

Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Dave Smith Instruments or Sequential. Nothing from the instrument is shipped: its programs and waves come from files you supply (see the README, "Your own sounds and waves").

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.
- MPC OS **3.x** (the skin format is newer than 2.15.1 reads).

## Install

manifest.name: MPC Commander addin
manifest.about: The plugins MPC loads, with their own skins, and MPC's transport, in a desktop app (through an SSH tunnel by default).

versions.notes:
The plugins MPC loads, with their own skins, and MPC's transport, in a desktop app (through an SSH tunnel by default).

## What's new in 1.1.0

- A Gen2 (aarch64) build, alongside the Gen1 (armv7) one (#3).
- Preload chaining fix: `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)` now searches the libraries loaded after the caller first, so Commander sits safely next to other addins that wrap the same functions (#1).

## Requirements

- An MPC OS standalone device. Pick the zip for yours:
  - `mpc-armv7`: Gen1 (MPC Live/Live II, One, X, Key 61/37, Force)
  - `mpc-aarch64`: Gen2 (Live III, One G2, Key(s) G2), new in this release and not yet tested on a device
  The installer refuses the wrong one.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Installing addins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-Commander-addin-1.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Commander-addin-1.1.0/install.sh`

The installer copies the addin into `/data/mpc-addins/commander/`, adds `mpc_commander_addin.so` to the `LD_PRELOAD` list of MPC's service
and **restarts MPC** (save your project first). The list is extended, never replaced: other addins and the
libraries the firmware preloads stay. Where no writable file sets the list (the unit is on the read-only root), one
drop-in shared by every addin sets it, `/etc/systemd/system/<service>.service.d/90-mpc-addins.conf`. Re-run the
installer after a firmware update. `-y` skips the question, `-n` leaves the restart to you.

Settings are in `/data/mpc-addins/commander/mpc_commander_addin.conf`; an upgrade keeps your edits.

It listens on the device only. From your computer: ssh -L 6730:127.0.0.1:6730 root@<device address>, then connect the MPC Commander desktop app to localhost:6730 (bind and port are in mpc_commander_addin.conf). For transport and MIDI, enable the MPC Commander port in MPC's MIDI preferences: as an input (with Receive MMC on) and as an output with clock sync and Send MMC.

Uninstalling and the file list are in `INSTALL.md` inside each zip.

plugins.author: mitchoster

manifest.name: MPC DJ FX 2
manifest.about: One-slot DJ insert: 3-band isolator, DJ filter, beat repeat, delay, reverb, flanger, grain delay (the original rack's Glitch stage) and a true-peak limiter, driven by the eight macros measured from Lenny Kiser's DJ-FX rack.

versions.notes:
Fixes 3.1.5, where the QR could not be opened by a finger.

`#bar` is `pointer-events: none` so swipes reach the canvas; the `PAIR …` span inherited it,
so a real tap hit the canvas and the QR never appeared. The line now opts back in
(`pointer-events: auto`), as the other two ports already did.

Checked with hit-testing rather than `element.click()`: `elementFromPoint` at the line's real
position returned `<canvas>` before and `<span id=pair>` after, and a click there toggles the
QR `none → block`.

Where the QR is: on the phone page (`http://<device-ip>:8102/`), not on the MPC screen —
tap the `PAIR <url>` line in the bottom bar.

manifest.name: MPC DJ FX 2
manifest.about: One-slot DJ insert: 3-band isolator, DJ filter, beat repeat, delay, reverb, flanger, grain delay and a true-peak limiter, driven by eight macros; with a companion screen served in the browser.

versions.notes:
**The plugin now serves its own panel** on the LAN, port 8102: four faces (MACRO, FILTER, REPEAT, DELAY), read and write, one browser tab per device. `DJF2_HTTP=0` disables the listener, `DJF2_HTTP_RW=0` makes it read-only, and writes need an `X-DJF2: 1` header so another web page cannot post to it.

**Switches.** The two-state controls (SYNC, PONG, FILL, MODE, LIMITER, EQ CURVE) never registered a touch: they were drawn in a strip outside the reachable area of the 1280x628 screen. They are rocker controls inside the panel now.

**Write path.** The companion's header check was case-sensitive, so a browser tap was refused with "missing X-DJF2 header" while curl worked. Fixed.

**Tempo.** `/state` now carries `bpm_seen`: 0 means the host never reported a tempo, and the panel shows `--` instead of a number. A VST2 plugin cannot otherwise tell "host says 120" from "no tempo, here is a default".

**Rack is the default interface.** The zip ships `Plugin Skins/` with rack (default), studio and classic; switch at INTERFACE on the PERFORM page.

The network capability flagged by the catalog checker is this listener: LAN only, one port, off by switch.

versions.notes:
## 3.1.0 — one plugin, three interfaces, switchable inside the plugin

The three interfaces now ship **in the plugin folder**. No second download, no reinstall:

| Interface | Look | Pages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Studio** (default) | display on top, parameter cards below (reference: 3dthc's Shapey) | MACROS · DJ FX · DJ FX 2 |
| **Classic** | ivory chassis, ink masthead, eight tabs | MACROS · DJ · REPEAT · DELAY · EQ · VERB · FLANGE · SETUP |
| **Rack** | anodised graphite bays (reference: MagicStino's PulyTek) | PERFORM · FX · TONE |

### Switching

**INTERFACE** sits on the MACROS page (Studio), the SETUP page (Classic) and the PERFORM page (Rack).
Pick one, then remove the plugin instance on the track and insert it again — MPC binds a skin when an
instance is inserted and has no reload call, so the change lands on the next insert. No restart, no
`MPC.settings` edit.

Why a running instance cannot be disturbed: the interfaces live in `Plugin Skins/{studio,classic,rack}/`
and differ only in the files MPC reads on insert (`TUI.json` plus the Q-Link banks). Switching copies
those two small JSON files — written to a `.tmp` name and renamed — and rewrites no image, so the
voices that are playing keep every texture they have loaded.

`Plugin Skins/ui.txt` records the active interface. A project or preset carrying an older value is
corrected from that file on load, so loading a preset can never flip the interface behind your back
(the new `ui` parameter is the 89th; appending it leaves existing projects and presets intact).

### Verified on the device (MPC Live II, MPC OS 3.x, 2026-10-28)

- Studio → Classic → Rack → Studio: each switch rewrote `TUI.json` + `Q-Links.json` and `ui.txt` to
  match, the running instance kept rendering, and the next insert came up with the chosen interface
  (Classic's ivory eight-tab skin and the Rack's graphite bays both confirmed on screen).
- `catalog_check --catalog` OK; host test PASSED; the switch mechanism was also driven offline against
  the real engine (a `state` load with an older `ui` value changes no file).

### Assets

One zip now. The three separate `…-ui-classic` / `…-ui-pulytek` zips stay available under **3.0.1** for
anyone who wants a single interface without the other two on disk (15 MB vs 0.7 MB).
