versions.notes:
## 3.0.0 — three interfaces, one plugin

The same `.so` and the same 88 parameters, shipped with three skins. Install the one you like; the plugin,
its sound and its presets are identical.

| Asset | Look | Pages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MPC-DJ-FX-2-3.0.0-mpc-armv7.zip` | **Studio** (default) | DJ FX · DJ FX 2 · SETUP |
| `MPC-DJ-FX-2-3.0.0-ui-classic.zip` | **Classic** (ivory, 8 tabs) | MACROS · DJ · REPEAT · DELAY · EQ · VERB · FLANGE · SETUP |
| `MPC-DJ-FX-2-3.0.0-ui-pulytek.zip` | **Rack** | PERFORM · FX · TONE |

Design references: **MagicStino — PulyTek** and **3dthc — Shapey 5-band EQ**. Composition only, no artwork
was copied.

### Engine and behaviour

- **Meter ballistics** rewritten: VU 0.4 s, repeat 0.5 s, delay tail 1.5 s, reverb tail 2.5 s. The old
  value was a ~40 s release, which made the meters look stuck at full.
- **PANIC zeroes the meters** immediately (it used to leave the last value standing).
- **VU CAL** (`vu_cal`, −12…+12 dB, 1 dB steps): trims which level reads full scale — after DubTape2's
  calibration trimmer.
- **MIX is a read-out** (`mix_show`): the wet mix is derived from the eight macros, so a knob there would be
  overwritten on the next macro move.
- **Q-Links per section** in the Studio skin: a tab's bank follows the cards in reading order, so the
  isolator's fourth knob is LOW X and no longer the DJ filter's LPF.

Checks: host test (x86, ASan/UBSan) PASSED; device bench PASS (worst p99 12.7 %, worst block 14.4 %);
`catalog_check --catalog` OK on all three zips; `tools/publish-check` clean on the source export.

versions.notes:
## 2.3.0 — ECHO switch, tab last, and a fix for the jumping preset list

- **DISPLAY switch** on the ECHO page (`ech_on`, Off/On, default On). Off parks every column at zero and stops
  the history: no parameter pushes, no repaints.
- **Tab order**: ECHO moved behind SETUP, so MACROS / DJ / REPEAT / DELAY / VERB keep the five visible tab slots.
- **Fix: the preset list no longer jumps.** The meters were option-list parameters, and the wrapper asks the host
  for an `UpdateDisplay` whenever an engine-reported parameter has options — with 21 meters reported up to 20 times
  a second that flooded MPC's parameter view. The meters are now plain numeric parameters (0…N-1, integer
  display) like PulyTek's VU, so a push reports the value and nothing re-lists.
- Nothing else changed; the audio path is untouched.

Measured on an MPC Live II with the display running: MPC process 152–154 % of one core on ECHO versus 136–168 %
on MACROS — the 16 columns at 5 Hz sit inside the noise. Sample and hold of the waterfall verified on the device.

Checks: host test (x86, ASan/UBSan) PASSED; device CPU bench PASS; 70 parameters.

versions.notes:
FileBrowser Quantum beside MPC: browse, upload and download the device's drives in a web browser (through an SSH tunnel by default).

## 1.0.0

The first stable release. It is the same as 0.1.1, which has been running on an MPC Key 37:

- FileBrowser Quantum v2.0.1-stable, the unmodified upstream binary. It starts with MPC and stops when MPC exits, at low CPU and disk priority, with no search index by default.
- It listens on `127.0.0.1:6760`: reach it through an SSH tunnel. `bind=0.0.0.0` opens it to the network.
- Log in as `admin`, password `mpcadmin`. Change it in FileBrowser or with `password=` in the settings. A change made in FileBrowser survives MPC restarts.
- It shows `/media` (Gen1's internal drive, SD cards and USB drives) and `/storage`, named Drives and Storage. On Gen1, Drives includes all of `/data`, MPC's settings among it.

Upgrading from 0.1.x keeps your settings, password and FileBrowser's database.

## Requirements

- An MPC OS standalone device. Pick the zip for yours:
  - `mpc-armv7`: Gen1 (MPC Live/Live II, One, X, Key 61/37, Force). Tested on an MPC Key 37, MPC OS 3.9.1.2
  - `mpc-aarch64`: Gen2 (Live III, One G2, Key(s) G2). Not yet tested on a device
  The installer refuses the wrong one.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Installing addins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-File-Browser-1.0.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-File-Browser-1.0.0/install.sh`

The installer copies the addin into `/data/mpc-addins/filebrowser/`, adds `mpc_filebrowser_addin.so` to the `LD_PRELOAD` list of MPC's service
and **restarts MPC** (save your project first). The list is extended, never replaced: other addins and the
libraries the firmware preloads stay. Where no writable file sets the list (the unit is on the read-only root), one
drop-in shared by every addin sets it, `/etc/systemd/system/<service>.service.d/90-mpc-addins.conf`. Re-run the
installer after a firmware update. `-y` skips the question, `-n` leaves the restart to you.

Settings are in `/data/mpc-addins/filebrowser/mpc_filebrowser_addin.conf`; an upgrade keeps your edits.

From a computer: ssh -N -L 6760:127.0.0.1:6760 root@<device>, then open http://localhost:6760 and log in as admin, password mpcadmin (change it there, or with password= in mpc_filebrowser_addin.conf).

Uninstalling and the file list are in `INSTALL.md` inside each zip.

This addin is MIT. FileBrowser Quantum is Apache-2.0, by its authors; its licence ships in each zip as `LICENSE-filebrowser`.

**Credits.** The companion screen follows [VADER](https://github.com/sunskiefer/VADER) by sunskiefer
(L'Cronx), which has served its plugin screen as a web page since v0.6.0 (2026-10-24) — the same reason
applies here: MPC draws plugin screens itself and every moving widget costs a redraw. Approach borrowed,
no code: this page is written against our own status feed and polls a small JSON document instead of
streaming WebSocket frames.

manifest.name: MPC Plaits

versions.notes:
Mutable Instruments Plaits as a native MPC OS VST2 instrument: all 24 models, up to 8 voices, LFOs, envelopes, cycle and random sources, a fixed and an assignable 4x4 mod matrix, tempo sync, and a six-page touchscreen skin with Q-Links.

## What's new in 1.0.1

- **About 12% less CPU on average**, up to ~30% on Snare Drum and Modal Resonator: the plugin is now built for the Cortex-A17 in Gen1 devices (`-mcpu=cortex-a17 -mfpu=neon-vfpv4 -O3 -funsafe-math-optimizations`).
- Fast Q-Link sweeps peak lower: p99 ~30% → ~24% of an audio block.
- No parameter changes: projects saved with 1.0.0 load as before. Pitched models sound the same; noise-driven models (Speech, Swarm, Particle, the drums) can render with slightly different random detail.

Upgrading: run the 1.0.1 installer over 1.0.0; it replaces the plugin in place.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on an MPC One with MPC OS 3.9.1. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-Plaits-1.0.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Plaits-1.0.1/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/poloq - VST - MPC Plaits/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **MPC Plaits** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Plaits-1.0.1/uninstall.sh` removes the plugin folder and the plugin-list entry (it also stops and
restarts MPC). Projects that use the plugin will load without it. Files you added yourself are kept.

## CPU

Measured on a Gen1 device (MPC Live/One/X/Force class, Cortex-A17) with `tools/bench.sh` from [mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins): worst p99 **23.7%** of one audio block, worst block 34.6%, verdict **WARN**. As a rule of thumb, several instances run comfortably when p99 is under 15%.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-Plaits-1.0.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Plaits-1.0.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/poloq - VST - MPC Plaits/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **MPC Plaits** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Plaits-1.0.0/uninstall.sh` removes the plugin folder and the plugin-list entry (it also stops and
restarts MPC). Projects that use the plugin will load without it. Files you added yourself are kept.

## Install by hand

1. Copy `portable/poloq - VST - MPC Plaits/` to `/sdcard/Synths/poloq - VST - MPC Plaits/`. It holds `plaits.so`, `plugin-meta.xml`, `version.xml`, `Plugin Skins/`
   and the data:
2. Stop MPC: `systemctl stop acvs`
3. Back up the settings file, `MPC.settings` (on a Force: `/media/az01-internal/Settings/MPC/MPC.settings`).
4. In `MPC.settings`, inside `<VALUE name="pluginList-arm"><KNOWNPLUGINS>`, add the line from `plugin-meta.xml` with
   `%payload-path%` replaced by `/sdcard/Synths`. If there is no `pluginList-arm` value yet, add one just before `</PROPERTIES>`:
   ```xml
   <VALUE name="pluginList-arm">
     <KNOWNPLUGINS>
       (the line from plugin-meta.xml)
     </KNOWNPLUGINS>
   </VALUE>
   ```
5. Start MPC: `systemctl start acvs`. If MPC shows default settings, restore your backup (the XML was malformed).

Edit `MPC.settings` only while MPC is stopped: MPC can save its own copy over a change made while it runs. Tools that
rebuild the whole plugin list from the plugin folders in `Synths` keep this plugin, because it is such a folder.

## CPU

Measured on a Gen1 device (MPC Live/One/X/Force class, Cortex-A17) with `tools/bench.sh` from [mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins): worst p99 **30.3%** of one audio block, worst block 38.7%, verdict **WARN**. As a rule of thumb, several instances run comfortably when p99 is under 15%.

## Files

On an MPC One or Live (SD card mounted `noexec`), install into an internal Synths folder listed in `MPC.settings`' `SynthContentLocations`: `sh install.sh -t /media/az01-internal/Synths`.

CPU (MPC One, tools/bench.sh): ~8% p99 of an audio block with 4-16 voices; a fast Q-Link sweep peaks at 30% p99 (WARN).

## What's new in 1.0.2

- **Press the device's hardware buttons** (#3). PLAY, STOP, REC, UNDO, MIXER, the arrows and the rest can now be pressed from the web page (a new button row), the HTTP API (`GET /buttons`, `GET /button?name=`) and MCP (`list_buttons`, `press_button`, `learn_button`).   - **Akai Force:** 22 buttons are built in and found automatically.
  - **Other devices:** start with no buttons. Run `learn_button`, press a button on the device, and it's saved under the name you give in `buttons.conf` next to the `.so`. You can edit that file, and an entry there overrides a built-in one.
  - Buttons that only work together with another (SHIFT, EDIT, COPY) do nothing when pressed alone from here.
- **Fixed: `send_midi` with `note_on` sent a note-off** (#2). It now sends a real note-on (`90 …`). `play_notes` was not affected.

The MPC screen in a browser, and an MCP server so an AI model can see and touch it, play MIDI and read files.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61 and Key 37).

- Installing addins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Remote-addin-1.0.2/install.sh`

The installer copies the addin into `/data/mpc-addins/remote/`, adds `mpc_remote_addin.so` to the `LD_PRELOAD` list of MPC's service
and **restarts MPC** (save your project first). The list is extended, never replaced: other addins and the
libraries the firmware preloads stay. Where no writable file sets the list (the unit is on the read-only root), one
drop-in shared by every addin sets it, `/etc/systemd/system/<service>.service.d/90-mpc-addins.conf`. Re-run the
installer after a firmware update. `-y` skips the question, `-n` leaves the restart to you.

It listens on the device only. From your computer: ssh -L 6720:127.0.0.1:6720 root@<device address>, then open http://localhost:6720 (bind and port are in mpc_remote_addin.conf).

versions.notes:
## 1.2.0 — one plugin, three interfaces, switchable inside the plugin

The three interfaces now ship **in the plugin folder**. No second download, no reinstall:

| Interface | Look | Pages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Studio** (default) | display panel on top, parameter cards below (reference: 3dthc's Shapey) | TAPE · SYNC OUT |
| **Classic** | RE-202-inspired ivory faceplate | MAIN · TAPE · OUT |
| **Rack** | anodised graphite bays (reference: MagicStino's PulyTek) | PROGRAM · TAPE · TONE |

**INTERFACE** is on the TAPE page's ECHO/VERB card (Studio), the OUT page (Classic) and at the bottom of
the PROGRAM/MIX bay (Rack). Pick one, then remove the plugin instance and insert it again — MPC binds a
skin at insert and has no reload call, so the change lands on the next insert.

Why a running instance cannot be disturbed: the interfaces live in `Plugin Skins/{studio,classic,rack}/`
and differ only in the files MPC reads on insert (`TUI.json` plus the Q-Link banks). Switching copies
those two small JSON files — written to a `.tmp` name and renamed — and rewrites no image.

`Plugin Skins/ui.txt` records the active interface; a project or preset carrying an older value is
corrected from disk on load, so a preset can never flip it. The selector is the 22nd parameter (21 engine
controls + `ui`), appended, so existing projects and presets load unchanged.

### Verified on the device (MPC Live II, MPC OS 3.x, 2026-10-28)

Studio → Classic → Rack: every tap rewrote `TUI.json` + `Q-Links.json` and `ui.txt` to match, the running
instance kept rendering, and the next insert came up with the chosen interface (Classic's ivory faceplate
and the Rack's graphite bays both seen on screen).

Nothing in the audio path changed: `vst/src/ported/**` is untouched. Bench **WARN** (worst p99 22.6 %,
worst block 23.7 %) — the same engine cost as 1.1.0. `catalog_check --catalog` OK.

### Assets

One zip now. The three `…-ui-classic` / `…-ui-rack` zips stay available under **1.1.0** for anyone who
wants a single interface on disk (0.7 MB instead of 11 MB).

manifest.name: MPC USB audio addin
manifest.about: The MPC as a USB audio interface: its outputs and inputs as channels on the computer, next to its MIDI ports.

versions.notes:
The MPC as a USB audio interface: its outputs and inputs as channels on the computer, next to its MIDI ports.

## Changes in 1.1.0

- **For devices where MPC builds no USB gadget in standalone mode** (an MPC One on HAKAI 3.9.1, #4; an MPC Live II on custom firmware, #1). After `own_wait` seconds (30) with no gadget at all, the addin builds its own, with only the audio function, so the computer sees a USB audio device but no MPC MIDI port. The addin gives the USB port back as soon as MPC enables a gadget of its own, and it also removes its gadget when MPC exits and at the next MPC start. `standalone_create=0` turns this off. Based on the patch and device findings in #4 by @shumiyao. This build has run on a Key 37 only, where MPC builds its gadget and the new code stays out of the way. It has not yet run on a device that needs it.
- **On HAKAI**, `/usr/bin/az01-launch-MPC` sets `LD_PRELOAD` itself, so the installer's setting doesn't reach MPC and the installer warns about it. Until the shared installer handles that launcher, add the library to the launcher's `LD_PRELOAD` lines by hand (README, "Limits").
- The installer is the current one from mpc-vst-plugins main.

## Requirements

- A Gen1 MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61 and Key 37). The installer refuses anything else.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Installing addins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-USB-audio-addin-1.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-USB-audio-addin-1.1.0/install.sh`

The installer copies the addin into `/data/mpc-addins/usb-audio/`, adds `libmpc_usb_audio.so` to the `LD_PRELOAD` list of MPC's service
and **restarts MPC** (save your project first). The list is extended, never replaced: other addins and the
libraries the firmware preloads stay. Where no writable file sets the list (the unit is on the read-only root), one
drop-in shared by every addin sets it, `/etc/systemd/system/<service>.service.d/90-mpc-addins.conf`. Re-run the
installer after a firmware update. `-y` skips the question, `-n` leaves the restart to you.

Settings are in `/data/mpc-addins/usb-audio/usbaudio.conf`; an upgrade keeps your edits.

Connect the MPC to a computer: it shows up as a USB audio device next to its MIDI ports. Log: usbaudio.log in this folder.

Uninstalling and the file list are in `INSTALL.md` inside each zip.

Mutable Instruments **Rings + Plaits** in one native MPC OS instrument — 20 engines, state-variable filter, reverb / tape delay / chorus / drive, 6 envelopes, 4 LFOs + mod matrix, velocity / mod-wheel / aftertouch, and a 5-page touchscreen skin with Q-Links.

> **0.9 preview.** Tested on an MPC One (Gen1). Other Gen1 devices (Live/X/Key/Force) run the same `MPC` program and are expected to work but are unverified.

## Requirements
- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live/Live II, One, X, Key 61).
- **Root shell (SSH)** access — a modded unit. Installing plugins this way is unofficial; back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install
1. Unzip, copy the folder to the device: `scp -r Mutable-Vibe-MPC-0.9.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Mutable-Vibe-MPC-0.9.0/install.sh`

The installer stops MPC (save your project first), installs the plugin + skin as one folder in `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, registers the plugin, and restarts MPC. Then add **Mutable Vibe MPC** to a track from the Instrument plugin browser. Full manual steps + uninstall are in the zip's `INSTALL.md`.

## Devices with a read-only `/sdcard` or an exfat (noexec) SD card
Some Hakai / MockbaMod MPC One setups mount `/sdcard` read-only and only read plugin skins from the exfat SD (`/media/MPCONE/Synths`, `noexec`) and firmware. There the portable installer can't place an executable `.so` where MPC loads it — install by hand with a **split layout** (`.so` to an executable path like `/data/vst/`, skin to the SD `Synths` folder, an explicit `pluginList-arm` entry). See the README's "Devices with a read-only /sdcard" section for the exact steps. (A different SD card doesn't change this — exfat is always `noexec`.)

manifest.name: NAM
manifest.about: Neural Amp Modeler captures as an MPC insert effect, with cab IR, tone, gate, pitch, delay, reverb and an on-device TONE3000 downloader.

versions.notes:
## What's new in 1.0.9

- **Works on MPC OS 2.x as well as 3.x.** The screen skin is now written in the MPC OS 2.x format, which 3.x reads too, so the touchscreen page draws on 2.x units instead of staying empty. Checked against MPC OS 2.15.1's own skins and shown working on a Key 37 (MPC OS 3.9.1); not yet tried on a 2.x unit, so reports from 2.x owners are welcome.
- **TONE3000 downloads follow the ARCH filter** (since 1.0.8): under the default `MPC` filter a pack saves only its Lite/Feather/Nano captures, so heavy captures that can't run in real time on the device aren't downloaded unless you switch ARCH yourself.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r NAM-1.0.9 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/NAM-1.0.9/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/jacob-sabella - VST - NAM/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Your own files go in `models/`, `cabs/`, `models-removed/`, `favorites.txt/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/jacob-sabella - VST - NAM/`); the installer keeps them when you upgrade and uninstall, and moves them there from the old `/sdcard/vst` location if you had installed the plugin that way.

Then add **NAM** to a track from the plugin browser (Insert effects). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

manifest.about: New take on the OP-1 nitro for MPC. 12 factory presets. Adds a MIX knob (dry to wet).

versions.notes:
Repackaged for the Open MPC plugin catalog. The plugin binaries are the same ones from 0.4.0. What changed is the packaging: catalog ids now start with `op1fx-` (for example `op1fx-delay`), the installer matches the current mpc-vst-plugins template, and the repo carries MPC screenshots and a `tested.json`.

Tested on an MPC Live III (Gen2), MPC OS 3.9.1. The armv7 zips (Gen1, Force, MPC One) are built but not tested on hardware yet.

Download `OP1-Suite-0.4.1-mpc-aarch64.zip` to install all twenty on a Gen2 MPC, or one plugin zip for a single plugin.

TAL-NoiseMaker: a classic virtual-analog polysynth with 256 factory presets.

## What's new in 1.1.1

Built on sd88me's fixed wrapper ([mpc-vst-plugins#499](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins/discussions/499)): on track edit → automation, the physical Q-Links move this plugin's parameters again (before, they didn't move or snapped straight back). Controls that change others, such as a preset, still redraw the screen. Nothing else changed: same parameters, sound and screen, and saved projects open as before.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r SYN-Noisemaker-1.1.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/SYN-Noisemaker-1.1.1/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/TAL - VST - [SYN] Noisemaker/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Your own files go in `noisemaker/presets/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/TAL - VST - [SYN] Noisemaker/`); the installer keeps them when you upgrade and uninstall, and moves them there from the old `/sdcard/vst` location if you had installed the plugin that way.

Then add **[SYN] Noisemaker** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

plugins.author: MrHighMan
plugins.summary: Multi-format sampler: plays Akai, E-mu, Roland, Kontakt/Maschine, SF2 and SFZ instruments straight from their files or sampler disk images, with layers, keyswitching, a mod matrix and its own screen skin.

versions.notes:
## Omni Sampler 1.8.1

### New
- **Korg Wavestation**: EX waves, all-data dumps, multi-bank files, split cards and VS single-cycle waves.
- **Wavetables**: Surge/Bitwig `.wt` and chunkless WAV wavetables (Serum, WaveEdit).
- **Ensoniq SD-1 / VFX-SD**: SysEx programs, played from the instrument's wave ROMs.
- **Gen2 support**: a new `aarch64` build for 64-bit MPCs (MPC Live III, MPC XL and kin). Thanks to @djru5h, who built it and confirmed it on his MPC XL (#7).

### Fixed
- **Q-Links on the automation screen**: on track edit → automation, Q-Links can now move Omni's parameters (rebuilt against the fixed mpc-vst-plugins wrapper, #6).
- Korg M1 reader fixes; README and INFO pages updated.

### Downloads
| Zip | For |
|---|---|
| `Omni-Sampler-1.8.1-mpc-armv7.zip` | Gen1: MPC Live / Live II / One / X / Force |
| `Omni-Sampler-1.8.1-mpc-aarch64.zip` | Gen2: MPC Live III / XL |

Install with the [MPC plugin installer](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins), or unzip, copy the folder to the MPC and run `sh install.sh` as root. On Gen2, external drives are mounted `noexec`, so install to the internal drive (`install.sh -t /nvme/Synths`). The zip's `INSTALL.md` has the full steps. Requires a modded unit with root access, MPC OS 3.x.

**SHA-256**
```
cb46a190f5d36f52f661210e4236683d5cbfee8e4f5642330baeec6968416d21  Omni-Sampler-1.8.1-mpc-armv7.zip
78e4241207b25934c8c7a623df953e8b21ac6840b79ee36931edfbd022c58fad  Omni-Sampler-1.8.1-mpc-aarch64.zip
```

See README for the 1.8.0 changes: Korg M1 / M1R / M1EX SysEx played from the M1 sample ROM dumps or Korg's M1 disk (programs, combinations, drum kits, all-data dumps, Plus+1 card), Korg TRITON content dumps and TRINITY banks, Trinity/Triton KMP/KSF/KSC, Ensoniq EPS/ASR disks, Yamaha Motif/Montage libraries, Logic EXS24, BIN/CUE images, FX page, browser groups and faster loading of big folders. Tested on MPC Live II.

- **PANIC** button (top right, on every page): one tap silences every sound within 5 ms and clears anything still held (keys, sustain pedal, the screen pads, pitch bend, mod wheel). Use it if a note ever hangs.

**Fix**
- Hanging notes: a note-off that arrived on a different MIDI channel than its note-on was ignored, so looped sounds (strings, pads) could ring forever. It now releases the note.

Projects and automation from 1.4 and 1.5 keep working (parameter indices are unchanged).

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Omni-Sampler-1.6.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Omni-Sampler-1.6.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, copies the files, then **stops MPC** (save your project first), backs up
`MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place.
Add `-y` to skip the confirmation prompt.

Then add **Omni Sampler** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Omni-Sampler-1.6.0/uninstall.sh` removes the files and the plugin-list entry (it also stops and
restarts MPC). Projects that use the plugin will load without it.

## Install by hand

1. Copy the files:
   - `payload/vst/omni_sampler.so` → `/sdcard/vst/omni_sampler.so`
- `payload/vst/omni-sampler/licenses` → `/sdcard/vst/omni-sampler/licenses`
   - `payload/Synths/MR HighMan - VST - Omni Sampler/` → `/sdcard/Synths/MR HighMan - VST - Omni Sampler/`
2. Stop MPC: `systemctl stop acvs`
3. Back up the settings file, `MPC.settings` (on a Force: `/media/az01-internal/Settings/MPC/MPC.settings`).
4. In `MPC.settings`, inside `<VALUE name="pluginList-arm"><KNOWNPLUGINS>`, add the line from `plugin.xml`.
   If there is no `pluginList-arm` value yet, add one just before `</PROPERTIES>`:
   ```xml
   <VALUE name="pluginList-arm">
     <KNOWNPLUGINS>
       (the line from plugin.xml)
     </KNOWNPLUGINS>
   </VALUE>
   ```
5. Start MPC: `systemctl start acvs`. If MPC shows default settings, restore your backup (the XML was malformed).

versions.notes:

With more than one place (the internal drive and an SSD or card, say) it names the drive (`CARD · 12.0 GB ▾`) and opens an **INSTALL TO** menu with each drive's free space; the choice is remembered. versions.notes:
**Open MPC Plugin Manager G2 0.2.1: it remembers where you install**

If your plugins live on an SSD or card instead of the user drive, you now choose it once and it sticks.

**What's new**
- **Remembers your install location.** When more than one place can take plugins, the restart prompt shows where the new ones will go with a CHANGE button. The place you confirm is now the default for new installs, so an SSD or card chosen once stays the default. If that drive is missing, the manager uses its normal default and keeps your choice for when the drive is back. Updates always stay where the plugin already is.
- **Cleans up after itself on restarts.** Each time the manager restarts MPC to apply changes, it also empties MPC's skin image cache (a RAM disk that only a reboot used to clear), so skins don't start drawing black patches after many restarts.
- A Gen1 and a Gen2 build in the same release, as before: `-mpc-armv7.zip` for Force, Live, One, X and Key, `-mpc-aarch64.zip` for the Live III and other 64-bit models.

**Upgrade:** run the new install.sh over the old one with `-t <your Synths folder>`; it upgrades in place.

Built on poloq's mpc-vst-manager. Credits and full feature list are in the README.

---

## Downloads

- `Plugin-Manager-G2-0.2.1-mpc-armv7.zip`: **Gen1** (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key)
- `Plugin-Manager-G2-0.2.1-mpc-aarch64.zip`: **Gen2** (64-bit: MPC Live III and the other 64-bit models)

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device: `scp -r Plugin-Manager-G2-0.2.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. As root, run: `sh /tmp/Plugin-Manager-G2-0.2.1/install.sh -t '<your Synths folder>'`

The installer stops MPC (save your project first), copies the plugin and its skin into your Synths folder, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place.

`<your Synths folder>` must be one of the folders listed under `SynthContentLocations` in `MPC.settings` (MPC draws a plugin's skin only from there). Typically `/sdcard/Synths` on a Force or Gen1 MPC, `/nvme/Synths` on a Live III, `/storage/Synths` on an MPC One Gen2. To see the list: `grep -A6 SynthContentLocations <your MPC.settings>` (`/data/Settings/MPC/MPC.settings` on Gen2, `/media/az01-internal/Settings/MPC/MPC.settings` on Gen1).

You need root shell access to the device for this first install. Then add **Plugin Manager G2** (VST, manufacturer OpenMPC) to an instrument track; the device needs a network connection for the catalog. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

Full instructions, installing by hand, and the credits are in `INSTALL.md` inside each zip and in the [README](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins/blob/main/tools/plugin_manager_g2/README.md).

Install, update and remove catalog plugins on the MPC itself. It's a plugin with its own touchscreen skin: no computer or USB stick once it's installed.

**Why it exists:** it's built on poloq's mpc-vst-manager (the concept, the whole working app, releases up to 1.2.0) and pulls in the best ideas from Eurikon's tool and real-device reports, as an official OpenMPC version that stays in step with the catalog and the official install methods. One release, both builds: Gen1 (32-bit: Force, Live, One, X, Key) and Gen2 (64-bit: Live III and kin).

**What it does**
- Browse Discover / Installed / Updates with search, filter, sort, five per page with thumbnails, Stable/Beta, High CPU and "Tested on" badges, and a details page
- Queue INSTALL, UPDATE, UPDATE ALL, REMOVE, then one APPLY and one restart; CHANGE picks where to install
- Safe: installs only where MPC will draw the skin; checks every zip's SHA-256, contents and your device (architecture, glibc, MPC OS) before MPC stops; if an install fails, the plugin folder and MPC.settings are put back and the screen says why
- Picks the right zip for your device (armv7 or aarch64)
- Local zips, REGISTER for folders MPC doesn't list, light/dark theme, install history, keeps your 10 newest settings backups, warns when MPC's image cache is filling

**Tested on** an MPC Live III (Gen2, OS 3.10) and a Force (Gen1). The MPC One layout comes from a user's report and is tested offline only.

**Install:** unzip, copy to the device, run install.sh -t <your Synths folder> as root (INSTALL.md has the steps).

versions.notes:
**Lower CPU on Gen2 (MPC Live III).** The emulator now runs on the Live III's fast cores (Cortex-A76) instead of drifting onto the slow ones (Cortex-A55), with the DSP and emulator threads each on a core of their own. Measured on a Live III with 8 voices held: about 29% of a core, was 40-57%.

versions.notes:
**Osirus for MPC 0.2.9**: no more crackle on heavy chords, favourites in MPC's PRESET menu, and `.syx` banks.

- **Headroom.** Heavy, high-velocity chords made the emulated Virus clip its own output (the crackle some of you heard, with DROPOUTS at 0). Osirus now keeps the Virus's channel volume at about 100 and gives the difference back after it, with a soft limiter, so ordinary patches sound as loud as before and hot ones no longer clip. There is no new control; OUTPUT LEVEL % is unchanged. PATCH VOLUME still helps on a very hot patch.
- **Favourites.** On the BANKS page, **+FAV** saves the current patch (with your knob changes) from any bank and **-FAV** removes the favourite that is loaded. Up to 64, kept in `osirus/favourites.dat`, listed in MPC's PRESET menu. A favourite made on another ROM model (A, B, C) is shown as `Name <C>` and is not loaded.
- **`.syx` banks.** SysEx bank dumps saved as `.syx` in `osirus/banks/` now load, as `.mid` ones do.
- A keyboard's volume slider (CC 7) can no longer undo the headroom.
- If the labels look old after updating, restart MPC (it caches skin pictures).

If it still crackles, please send: the patch name, your MPC model and OS version, the buffer size, and the PLAY page STATS line (DROPOUTS n). DROPOUTS above 0 is a different problem from clipping.

No ROM is included. GPL-3.0, see CREDITS.md. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Access Music.

versions.notes:
# OTTmpc 1.0.0

Vital's OTT multiband up/down compressor ([vitOTTx](https://github.com/Sakhnovkrg/vitOTTx)'s DSP) as an **insert effect** for MPC OS standalone devices, with an OTT-style touchscreen skin, live per-band input/output meters with dB numbers, 12 Q-Link controls and 10 presets in MPC's PRESET menu.

![OTTmpc on a Force](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-OTT/claude/friendly-wozniak-m9ak1l/docs/screenshot.png)

- Controls: Depth, Time, In Gain, Out Gain, Upward, Downward, Mix, High/Mid/Low band gain, Low/Mid and Mid/High crossover.
- Presets: OTT Default, Flat (Bypass-ish), Gentle Glue, Parallel Smash, Upward Only, Downward Only, Drum Bus, Vocal Air, Bass Tighten, Lo-Fi Squash.
- CPU on a Force: worst p99 5.3% of an audio block (PASS).
- MPC OS 3.x only (the skin format needs it). GPL-3.0, as upstream.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61). The installer refuses anything else.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.
- Tested on a Force. Other models are untested.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the folder to the device: `scp -r OTTmpc-1.0.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/OTTmpc-1.0.0/install.sh` (stops MPC: save your project first)
3. Add **OTTmpc** to a track from the plugin browser (Insert effects).

Uninstall with `uninstall.sh` in the same folder. Full steps, including a manual install, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

plugins.name: Percolator
plugins.author: saustin2010
plugins.summary: Four-voice percussion synth laid out like the Erica Synths Pērkons HD-01 (three algorithms per voice, BBD delay, LFO to every knob), with envelope displays; each voice on its own MIDI channel with the Pērkons' CCs, and on its own track with Percolator OUT; plays the Pērkons' free kit packs.

manifest.name: [DRUM] Percolator
manifest.about: Four-voice percussion synth laid out like the Erica Synths Pērkons HD-01, with envelope displays; it plays the Pērkons' free kit packs.

versions.notes:
Four-voice percussion synth laid out like the Erica Synths Pērkons HD-01, with envelope displays; it plays the Pērkons' free kit packs.

## What's new in 2.1.0

**Your own samples on every voice.** SOURCE on each voice page switches it from its algorithm to a WAV file of your own (TUNE, DECAY, CRUSH, START or SLICE, then the voice's filter, drive and sends as ever). The SAMPLES page is Incipience's browser: PERCOLATOR FOLDER and the MPC's drives, a folder and its subfolders in one list, PREVIEW, LOAD or AUTO LOAD.

**RANDOMISE per voice**, beside SOURCE.

**Voices stop when their hit has died away** (before, only SNARE did, and a finished voice kept costing CPU), and a sample's end lets the filter and DRIVE ring out instead of clicking.

**Built on sd88me's fixed wrapper** ([mpc-vst-plugins#499](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins/discussions/499)): on track edit → automation, the physical Q-Links move Percolator's parameters again.

44 parameters are added at the end, so projects saved with 2.0.1 open with every voice on SYNTH and sound as before. Released with [FX] Percolator OUT 2.1.0 (its version, and the fixed wrapper).

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r DRUM-Percolator-2.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/DRUM-Percolator-2.1.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/Steve A - VST - [DRUM] Percolator/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Your own files go in `percolator/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/Steve A - VST - [DRUM] Percolator/`); the installer keeps them when you upgrade and uninstall, and moves them there from the old `/sdcard/vst` location if you had installed the plugin that way.

Then add **[DRUM] Percolator** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

manifest.about: Four-voice percussion synth laid out like the Erica Synths Pērkons HD-01, with envelope displays; it plays the Pērkons' free kit packs.

versions.notes:
Four-voice percussion synth laid out like the Erica Synths Pērkons HD-01, with envelope displays; it plays the Pērkons' free kit packs.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r DRUM-Percolator-1.0.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/DRUM-Percolator-1.0.1/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/Steve A - VST - [DRUM] Percolator/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Your own files go in `percolator/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/Steve A - VST - [DRUM] Percolator/`); the installer keeps them when you upgrade and uninstall, and moves them there from the old `/sdcard/vst` location if you had installed the plugin that way.

Then add **[DRUM] Percolator** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

plugins.summary: Valley Audio's Plateau reverb from VCV Rack, patched: every CV input on a built-in source (four Bogaudio LFOs, Tidal Modulator 2, Random Sampler, step and gate sequencers) synced to the MPC tempo, a brickwall limiter, Panic and 16 presets, each page drawn like its module.

manifest.name: PlateauXXL
manifest.about: PlateauXXL by L'Cronx: Valley Audio's Plateau reverb for MPC OS

versions.notes:
> **0.4.3** is 0.4.2 built on the latest wrapper and includes the Q-Link and automation fix (#486–#489): Q-Links now move parameters on the track's automation screen. Nothing else changed. Installs over 0.4.2 in place.

**PlateauXXL — Valley Audio's Plateau reverb, patched with its own LFOs, random sources and sequencers, running natively inside MPC OS on the Akai Force.**

Put it on a track, a submix or the master: huge Dattorro plate tails, Hold to freeze the tank, Clear to empty it, Tuned mode for pitched resonances, and every one of the module's 15 CV jacks patched to a modulation source running inside the plugin. Everything sits in one insert slot, with its own touchscreen pages and Q-Links, follows the MPC tempo and saves with your project.

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Profit-5-0.2.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`

manifest.name: PulyTek
manifest.about: Experimental Pultec-style WDF EQ. Hardware validation pending.

versions.notes:
PulyTek is a separate open-source Pultec-style EQ port for the native Akai Force/MPC Gen1 OpenPlugin format.

- Blue vintage panel, Bakelite-style knobs, ribbed selector buttons, warm lamps and stereo VU meters.
- Upstream EQP-WDF-1A passive WDF circuit by Alberto Barrera / ABSounds, GPLv3.
- Extra tube-colour switch with DRIVE, WARMTH and continuous wet/dry MIX, six-frequency AIR shelf with one continuous AMOUNT control, output trim and full bypass.
- Side Mixing on/off, 0–200% stereo width, side level and four side-only parametric bands.
- Native ARMv7 hard-float VST2 effect, Akai TUI skin, Q-Link mappings, portable installer and complete corresponding source.

**The maintainer reports hardware testing of the preceding plugin version. This release’s new LED touch behavior still needs device verification; a detailed device/firmware record and CPU benchmark are pending.**
Desktop DSP and native host tests passed with sanitizers. ARM loading/audio/state passed under QEMU with Force 3.9.1
system libraries; that is not a physical-device compatibility guarantee. Read README.md and docs/VALIDATION.md.

The portable ZIP is for Force/MPC; the optional desktop Linux VST3 is a separate CI artifact and is not installed on Force.

0.1.0-rc2 adds a combined Tube & AIR page with Drive and Mix controls. Legacy rc1 tube/EQ state chunks load with the original +3 dB, fully wet AIR defaults.

0.1.0-rc3 removes the redundant AIR Mix knob, renames AIR Drive to Amount and turns AIR off below 2%. Tube controls are unchanged. Legacy native state migrates; rc2 partial AIR mixes preserve high-frequency gain approximately through the shelf transition.

49 original factory programs: Init and six each for Voice, Drums, Bass, Guitar, Keys, Bus, Master and Stereo. Native PRESET menu and desktop VST3 program support; complete control recall, including AIR amount before enable. Includes Drums Smash Bassdrum and Master Light / Hard Colour / Air / Smile / Warm / Wide Polish.

0.1.0-rc4 corrects VU metering: sine-calibrated rectified averaging, two-pole needle inertia (approximately 300 ms to 99%), symmetric smooth return, 20 Hz visual updates and voltage-proportional scale spacing. The clearly labelled programme reference is now 0 VU = -9 dBFS RMS, to avoid pinning on louder samples. +3 VU is -6 dBFS RMS-equivalent; sustained levels above that still legitimately reach the stop. Audio processing and preset settings are unchanged.

Global OUTPUT COMP is beside the stereo meters. It reuses the existing final output parameter and preserves preset/project gains; metering follows it.

1.0.0 makes AIR enable independent of Amount at every setting, including 0%. All LED lamps toggle on touch; POWER toggles global bypass and lights when processing is active. Tube, AIR and Side lamps toggle their own sections. Existing project and preset parameter keys are unchanged.

## Interface previews
Generated native interface previews, not device captures.

![Equalizer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagicStino/pulytek/v1.0.0/docs/preview_0.png)

![Tube and AIR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagicStino/pulytek/v1.0.0/docs/preview_1.png)

![Side Mixing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagicStino/pulytek/v1.0.0/docs/preview_2.png)

## 1.0.1 — stable preset popup during playback
VU values now notify the host without requesting a full display rebuild. This prevents the PRESET menu from repeatedly rebuilding while needles move. Preset selection still requests a redraw and recalls all controls. Audio processing, state keys and factory programs are unchanged. A dedicated host regression test verifies ongoing meter notifications, zero meter-driven display rebuilds and normal preset selection redraw. Physical popup confirmation remains pending.

plugins.name: RMXXXL
plugins.author: L'Cronx
plugins.summary: RMX-1000-style remix effect: isolator, DJ filter, Build Up / Break Down scenes, synced echo, Release FX and a Release kill switch, EQ Kill buttons, a clean Panic, Clouds, Dragonfly reverbs, sample pads with ADSR, 16 user presets and a brickwall limiter, with a big-button touchscreen skin and Q-Links.

manifest.name: RMXXXL
manifest.about: RMXXXL v.1 by L'Cronx: RMX-style remix FX for MPC OS

versions.notes:
> **1.2.3** is 1.2.2 built on the latest wrapper and includes the Q-Link and automation fix (#486–#489): Q-Links now move parameters on the track's automation screen. Nothing else changed. Installs over 1.2.2 in place.

**RMXXXL v.1 — an RMX-1000-style remix effect that runs natively inside MPC OS on the Akai Force.**

Put it on a track, a submix or the master and play the mix live: build-ups, breakdowns, filter sweeps, band kills, echoes, reverb washes, granular textures, drum and sample pads, a Release kill switch that drops everything back to dry, and a Panic button. Everything sits in one insert slot, with its own touchscreen pages and Q-Link sets.

> ✅ **1.2.1 is tested on an Akai Force** (MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod). It fixes the big knobs (they slid instead of turning in 1.2.0), puts the Q-Links in screen order (top row = bank 1, bottom row = bank 2), makes switches flip with a small Q-Link turn, stops lists like Beats from skipping, and keeps the dry level when Clouds is on. 1.2.0 was tested on an Akai Force (MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod) and fixes what the first Force test (1.1.1, MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod) found: screen pads and buttons now fire on every tap, option lists are readable, Q-Links no longer race through lists, controls are bigger. New: Release kill switch, separate Release FX button, Panic, 16 user presets, riser Tune / Duck. As with any third-party plugin, save your projects before installing, and report problems under **Issues**. Full list: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sunskiefer/RMXXXL/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## How you play it
1. **Shape the mix** with the isolator (Low / Mid / High, fully left = kill) and the DJ filter (left = low-pass, right = high-pass).
2. **Build tension** with **Build Up** (rising high-pass, echo, reverb and noise riser) or **Break Down** (closing low-pass washed into echo and reverb). One knob each.
3. **Drop it** with **Release FX**: Echo Out, Vinyl Brake or Backspin over 1/2 to 4 beats; it latches the scene off until both knobs are back at zero, like the RMX. Or switch **Release** on to kill everything to dry (Hard or Smooth) and off to bring it all back as it was.
4. **Add texture** with Clouds (six granular modes) and Dragonfly Plate, Room or Hall reverb.
5. **Hit the pads** from the screen, latching rolls or a MIDI track: built-in kick, snare, clap and hat, or your own WAV one-shots, each with its own ADSR.
6. **Stay safe**: a look-ahead brickwall limiter keeps the output under your Ceiling, and **Panic** puts everything back to factory settings in one tap.
7. **Save your scenes** in 16 preset slots (pads included).

Everything follows the MPC tempo, and all settings save with your project.

## Pages
**REMIX** (performance) · **CLOUDS** · **REVERB / PADS** · **PADS** · **SETUP** (limiter, crossovers, scene ranges, presets, riser)

## Requirements
- Akai Force (first generation); other Gen1 MPC OS units should work but are untested
- MPC OS 3.x
- Root SSH access (for example MockbaMod)

## Install
Download **RMXXXL-1.2.1-mpc-armv7.zip** below, unzip it, then:

    scp -r RMXXXL-1.2.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/
    ssh -t root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/RMXXXL-1.2.1/install.sh

The installer stops MPC (save first), installs the plugin, and starts MPC again. Then insert **RMXXXL** (manufacturer L'Cronx) as an insert effect. Pad samples go in `/sdcard/RMXXXL Samples`, presets in `/sdcard/RMXXXL Presets`.

## Play it from a MIDI track
RMXXXL opens its own MIDI port, **RMXXXL 1**. Create a MIDI track, set its MIDI output port to **RMXXXL 1**, and play: from MIDI Root (default 36 = C1) +0..+3 are Pads 1-4, +4..+7 the same pads as rolls while held, +8 Release FX, +9 Release on/off, +10 Panic. Step by step in the README and in INSTALL.md inside the zip.

Full guide (every control, MIDI setup, Q-Links, samples, presets, troubleshooting): [docs/USER_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/sunskiefer/RMXXXL/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md)

## Credits
- **Isolator and filter:** designs after the Mixxx project's LR8 isolator and filter effect
- **Clouds:** Emilie Gillet (Mutable Instruments), with Matthias Puech's Parasites firmware; MPC OS port and MIDI input by FullPace ([overcast](https://github.com/FullPace/overcast))
- **Reverbs:** Dragonfly Reverb by Michael Willis and Rob van den Berg, built on freeverb3 by Teru Kamogashira; MPC OS port by gmorb ([mpc-vst-dragonfly](https://github.com/gmorb/mpc-vst-dragonfly))
- **Plugin framework, skin tools and installer:** sd88me ([mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins))
- **Interface font:** Titillium Web (SIL Open Font License)

Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later.

manifest.name: RMXXXL
manifest.about: RMXXXL v.1 by ANDREALPHEUS: RMX-style remix FX for MPC OS

versions.notes:
**RMXXXL v.1 — an RMX-1000-style remix effect that runs natively inside MPC OS on the Akai Force.**

Put it on a track, a submix or the master and play the mix live: build-ups, breakdowns, filter sweeps, band kills, echoes, reverb washes, granular textures, drum and sample pads, a Release kill switch that drops everything back to dry, and a Panic button. Everything sits in one insert slot, with its own touchscreen pages and Q-Link sets.

> ✅ **1.2.1 is tested on an Akai Force** (MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod). It fixes the big knobs (they slid instead of turning in 1.2.0), puts the Q-Links in screen order (top row = bank 1, bottom row = bank 2), makes switches flip with a small Q-Link turn, stops lists like Beats from skipping, and keeps the dry level when Clouds is on. 1.2.0 was tested on an Akai Force (MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod) and fixes what the first Force test (1.1.1, MPC OS 3.9.1 with MockbaMod) found: screen pads and buttons now fire on every tap, option lists are readable, Q-Links no longer race through lists, controls are bigger. New: Release kill switch, separate Release FX button, Panic, 16 user presets, riser Tune / Duck. As with any third-party plugin, save your projects before installing, and report problems under **Issues**. Full list: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sunskiefer/RMXXXL/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## How you play it
1. **Shape the mix** with the isolator (Low / Mid / High, fully left = kill) and the DJ filter (left = low-pass, right = high-pass).
2. **Build tension** with **Build Up** (rising high-pass, echo, reverb and noise riser) or **Break Down** (closing low-pass washed into echo and reverb). One knob each.
3. **Drop it** with **Release FX**: Echo Out, Vinyl Brake or Backspin over 1/2 to 4 beats; it latches the scene off until both knobs are back at zero, like the RMX. Or switch **Release** on to kill everything to dry (Hard or Smooth) and off to bring it all back as it was.
4. **Add texture** with Clouds (six granular modes) and Dragonfly Plate, Room or Hall reverb.
5. **Hit the pads** from the screen, latching rolls or a MIDI track: built-in kick, snare, clap and hat, or your own WAV one-shots, each with its own ADSR.
6. **Stay safe**: a look-ahead brickwall limiter keeps the output under your Ceiling, and **Panic** puts everything back to factory settings in one tap.
7. **Save your scenes** in 16 preset slots (pads included).

Everything follows the MPC tempo, and all settings save with your project.

## Pages
**REMIX** (performance) · **CLOUDS** · **REVERB / PADS** · **PADS** · **SETUP** (limiter, crossovers, scene ranges, presets, riser)

## Requirements
- Akai Force (first generation); other Gen1 MPC OS units should work but are untested
- MPC OS 3.x
- Root SSH access (for example MockbaMod)

## Install
Download **RMXXXL-1.2.1-mpc-armv7.zip** below, unzip it, then:

    scp -r RMXXXL-1.2.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/
    ssh -t root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/RMXXXL-1.2.1/install.sh

The installer stops MPC (save first), installs the plugin, and starts MPC again. Then insert **RMXXXL** (manufacturer ANDREALPHEUS) as an insert effect. Pad samples go in `/sdcard/RMXXXL Samples`, presets in `/sdcard/RMXXXL Presets`.

## Play it from a MIDI track
RMXXXL opens its own MIDI port, **RMXXXL 1**. Create a MIDI track, set its MIDI output port to **RMXXXL 1**, and play: from MIDI Root (default 36 = C1) +0..+3 are Pads 1-4, +4..+7 the same pads as rolls while held, +8 Release FX, +9 Release on/off, +10 Panic. Step by step in the README and in INSTALL.md inside the zip.

Full guide (every control, MIDI setup, Q-Links, samples, presets, troubleshooting): [docs/USER_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/sunskiefer/RMXXXL/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md)

- **Plugin framework, skin tools and installer:** sd88me ([mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins))

manifest.name: setBfree Organ
manifest.about: Native tonewheel organ with drawbars, rotary speaker, effects and keyboard splits.

versions.notes:
![setBfree Organ 0.3.0 UPPER screen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SamplingHigh/mpc-vst-setbfree/v0.3.0/docs/images/setbfree-organ.png)

setBfree Organ 0.3.0 expands the native Force/MPC touchscreen interface to five pages and keeps the existing parameter indexes compatible with saved projects.

### Changes

- New `FX` page with extended overdrive and reverb controls.
- New upper, lower and pedal manual-level controls, all defaulting to 60%.
- Sustain pedal can switch between Leslie speed control and note sustain.
- Reworked UPPER and LOWER/PEDAL performance pages, including per-manual seven-position vibrato/chorus selectors.
- Three visible pedal drawbars: 16', 8' and 4'.
- Larger labels, custom toggle artwork, traditional drawbar colours and position-dependent drawbar grooves.
- Local Skin Studio and one-click skin updater scripts are included for layout customisation.
- Nine new parameters were appended to `params.lock`; existing indexes and project compatibility remain unchanged (`Compat 0`).

### CPU note

The normal audio path measured **8.9% p99 / 12.4% worst block at 16 voices** on an Akai Force. The generic benchmark's Q-Link stage reports `FAIL` because it also sweeps the four crosstalk controls: each of those intentionally rebuilds the setBfree organ core and can briefly mute audio. They live on the SETTINGS page and are intended for sound setup, not performance automation.

### Requirements and installation

- First-generation 32-bit ARM MPC OS device such as Force, Live/Live II, One, X or Key 61.
- MPC OS 3.x and root SSH access on a modded device.
- Save the current project before installing because the installer restarts MPC.

Unzip the download, copy the complete `setBfree-Organ-0.3.0` folder to the device, then run:

```sh
ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/setBfree-Organ-0.3.0/install.sh
```

The package includes complete GPL-2.0-or-later source provenance and portable install/uninstall scripts.

SHA-256: `CCF2876CD7E3B160C1FFEBE77E8534F05E537F206BC983749B1C03582E143378`

### Experimental Gen2 build

An additional **aarch64/Gen2** build is available as `setBfree-Organ-0.3.0-gen2-experimental.zip`.

- It uses the same plugin UID, parameter indexes and project-state format as the Gen1/Force build.
- The ARM64 functional host test and package validation pass, and the highest required GLIBC symbol is 2.29.
- It has **not been tested on physical Gen2 hardware**. Installation, audio, touchscreen rendering, Q-Links and project recall still need device confirmation.
- The non-standard asset name is intentional: this experimental build is not advertised through the public MPC VST catalog yet.
- Gen2 installation needs root access and a writable removable-media Synths folder, for example: `sh install.sh -t /media/<label>/Synths`.

SHA-256: `a4b0270f3a27d32d40ef4f0776407cc4ae6bd72627a2249916a06d6021ab92d8`

versions.notes:
The [sfizz](https://github.com/sfztools/sfizz) 1.2.3 SFZ sampler as a native instrument plugin for MPC OS standalone
hardware: SFZ libraries streamed from SD cards and USB drives, key switches, the instrument's own CC controls and Scala
tuning, on a one-page screen modelled on sfizz's own editor.

## Download the zip for your device
| Device | Zip |
|---|---|
| **Gen1**: MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61, Force (RK3288, 32-bit) | `sfizz-1.1.0-mpc-armv7.zip` |
| **Gen2**: MPC Live III and other RK3588 units (64-bit) | `sfizz-1.1.0-mpc-aarch64.zip` |
| **Gen1** with `vstscanner.sh` (Force VST distribution, e.g. MockbaMod) | `sfizz-for-MPC-OS-1.1.0.zip` |

Same plugin, screen, parameters and ID on both: projects move between generations. Needs MPC OS 3.x and root SSH access.
The installer zips check that they match the device. The manual is attached (`sfizz-for-MPC-OS-1.1.0-manual.pdf`).

## Install
**Installer zips** (`-mpc-armv7` / `-mpc-aarch64`):
```
scp -r sfizz-1.1.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/
ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/sfizz-1.1.0/install.sh      # stops and restarts MPC: save first
```
**Standalone zip with `vstscanner`** (Gen1): copy the `sfztools - VST - sfizz` folder into your card's `Synths` folder
next to `vstscanner.sh`, run the one-line preset fix from its README, then `vstscanner`. The README covers MockbaMod and
other firmware. Use one method per device: the scanner rebuilds MPC's whole plugin list.

Then add **sfizz** from the plugin browser (manufacturer "sfztools"), or from Sounds › INSTRUMENTS (the sfizz tile,
then Default).

## New in 1.1.0
- **Gen2 build** (aarch64): a native 64-bit build of the same engine. A new sfizz on Gen2 starts with Sample quality
  Sinc 8, Oscillator quality High and 96 voices (Gen1: Linear, Linear, 64), may keep up to 1 GB of decoded samples
  (Gen1: 384 MB) and streams 2 s ahead of each note (Gen1: 1.25 s). Measured offline, Sinc 8 costs about 1.3× Linear's
  CPU per voice there, about a third of what upstream sfizz needs on the same CPU. The Gen2 build has been tested
  on an MPC Live III (Gen2).
- **Larger drop-down lists**: taller rows, bigger text and wider cells in every option list, easier to read and hit.
- **Larger SFZ browser** (the file box's ⌄): six bigger rows per page, bigger text and buttons.
- **Larger navigation arrows**: the file box's ‹ › ⌄ and the browser's page arrows are bigger and easier to hit.
- **Standalone zip** for `vstscanner.sh` setups, with a README for MockbaMod and other firmware.

Full history: [RELEASE_NOTES.md](https://github.com/gmorb/mpc-vst-sfizz/blob/v1.1.0/RELEASE_NOTES.md). Tests:
[TESTING.md](https://github.com/§±secret(GITHUB_USERNAME)/mpc-vst-sfizz/blob/v1.1.0/TESTING.md).

6e1a0531226436cc0ad4b17f3a2e20e2e7c369bf828a2a6294ea193bab11f2ea  sfizz-for-MPC-OS-1.1.0.zip
eafbcad326993d5c113e9b05e0e60ed478587179255960657b4d492939dbb4f1  sfizz-for-MPC-OS-1.1.0-manual.pdf

## Requirements

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Shapey-5-Band-EQ-1.0.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`

and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **Shapey 5-Band EQ** to a track from the plugin browser (Insert effects). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

StepRunner-8: an 8-track, 64-step sequencer for MPC standalone with step conditions, step and CC locks, patterns, states and performance effects, driving a drum program over MIDI (ALSA port StepRunner-8).

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r StepRunner-8-1.2.0 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/StepRunner-8-1.2.0/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/djokenzi - VST - StepRunner-8/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **StepRunner-8** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

## What's New in 1.2.0

- **Eight CCs per track**: CC 6, CC 7 and CC 8 added
- **TRACK VALUES**: the track's own velocity, length, pan, probability and CC base values on one page
- **BFWD direction** and **SHIFT ◀ / ▶** in TRACK EDIT and PATTERN EDIT
- **Two Euclidean generators (A and B)**, combined with XOR / OR / AND / SUB
- **Second page of random tools**: RND / CLR COND, TIMING and RATCHETS
- **STOP CC** pad on PERFORM
- **TRACK SETUP** without READ / DISCARD / COMMIT, with IN USE warnings
- Smaller knob text, short CC names and an updated manual

---

### Eight CCs per track
CC 6, CC 7 and CC 8 join CC 1–5. They have step locks, PERFORM ALL offsets, RND CC 6–8 and CLR CC 6–8 buttons, and
Q-Links (12 on PROGRAM and PERFORM). CREATE DEFAULT MAP also maps CC 6 / CC 7 to the pad's Send 3 / Send 4.
FETCH CC VALUES now reads the pad's own saved values.

### TRACK VALUES
A new page in TRACK EDIT, laid out like STEP LOCKS. It holds the track's velocity, length, pan, probability and the
base values of CC 1–8. While it is open, the Q-Links control the track instead of the selected steps.

### BFWD direction and SHIFT
TRACK EDIT has a new direction, BFWD (back and forth, starting backwards). BOTH is now called FBWD.
SHIFT ◀ / ▶ rotates the track's steps by one, with all their locks. In PATTERN EDIT it rotates all 8 tracks.

### Two Euclidean generators
EUCLIDIAN has generator A on page 1 and generator B on page 2. Each has ENABLE, RANDOM, PULSE, ROTATE and LENGTH.
When both are on, XOR / OR / AND / SUB on page 2 combine their rhythms.

### Second page of random tools
The ◀ / ▶ arrows in PATTERN, TRACK and STEP EDIT open a second page with RND COND, RND TIMING and RND RATCHETS, and
their CLR versions. They act on the track (TRACK EDIT), on all 8 tracks (PATTERN EDIT) or on the selected steps
(STEP EDIT). RND RATCHETS also picks a ratchet resolution.

### STOP CC
A new PERFORM pad. While it is on, no CCs are sent and notes keep playing. When it is switched off, every track goes
back to its base values. NO LOCKS moved next to STOP CC. STATEs now recall only the effects that have a pad.

### TRACK SETUP
MIDI channel, note and the numbers of CC 1–8 take effect at once. The READ / DISCARD / COMMIT buttons are gone; tap
SETUP to leave. A red IN USE tag marks a CC number that is already used elsewhere.

### Smaller changes
- The knob value text is smaller and CC names are cut to 6 characters ("Filter Cutoff" → "F. Cut"), so the text of
  neighbouring knobs no longer overlaps.
- A STEP LOCKS knob with no lock shows the track's value in brackets and stays at "--" when turned down.
- The TIMING knobs are named Ratchets / Resolution. A shift back onto the grid shows "On Grid".
- The manual has new screenshots and covers every new page.

Projects saved with 1.1.x load unchanged.

---

versions.notes:
StepRunner-8: an 8-track, 64-step sequencer for MPC standalone with step conditions, step and CC locks, patterns, states and performance effects, driving a drum program over MIDI (ALSA port StepRunner-8).

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r StepRunner-8-1.0.2 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/StepRunner-8-1.0.2/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/djokenzi - VST - StepRunner-8/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **StepRunner-8** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

plugins.name: Stompbox
plugins.author: jacob-sabella
plugins.summary: A whole guitar rig from guitarix's DSP: gate, comp, wah, any number of pedals, amp, tone stack, power amp, cabinet with an IR loader, post FX, mod, delay, reverb and EQ. 219 models and guitarix's 40 factory presets in the PRESET menu. Not affiliated with guitarix.

manifest.name: Stompbox
manifest.about: A guitar rig as one insert effect: gate, compressor, wah, any number of pedals, amp, tone stack, power amp, cabinet, post FX, modulation, delay, reverb and EQ, from the guitarix project's DSP, with guitarix's 40 factory presets.

versions.notes:
> **Not a guitarix project.** I'm not affiliated with the guitarix developers. Stompbox was built with AI; please report problems [here](https://github.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-vst-stompbox/issues), not to guitarix.

First release.

- **Tested:** the `-mpc-armv7.zip` (Gen1) installed with its own `install.sh` on an MPC Key 37, MPC OS 3.9.1.2 (2026-10-26). The `-mpc-aarch64.zip` (Gen2) is tested offline only.
- **CPU:** the bench verdict is **WARN**: 13.5% of a block at p99 while playing the starting rig, 21.3% while every Q-Link is swept. Plan on one or two instances in a project. Heavier presets cost more (Convolv: 36% at p99); the README's CPU section has the figures.
- **Use a track insert.** On a silent drum pad, MPC doesn't run the insert, so the page and preset picks only catch up when the pad plays.

versions.notes:
Changes in 0.1.1: the SOUND page fills the page with bigger names and values, the pickers are sized for bank, sound and status text, the kit page is a popup menu; the OUTPUT tab follows the envelope tabs; distortion keeps a little more of its own gain.

Six-voice analog-style drum and synth voice for Akai MPC OS standalone devices (Force, MPC Live / One / X / Key), modelled on a classic drum machine's voice: two analog oscillators (saw, triangle, saw-tri, pulse) with sync and a sub oscillator, two sample oscillators that can bypass the filters, a resonant 2/4-pole lowpass that rings on its own, a highpass, feedback, five envelopes with delay and peak hold, two LFOs and eight modulation paths. A sound is the instrument's own 127 fields, so its sound and project SysEx dumps load as they are. New in the output section: **Distortion** (antialiased, level-matched), **Compress** with its envelope controls, and the mixer's **Delay**, which plays repeated notes as the original does. Kit mode plays 16 pads as 16 sounds. Native MPC screen skin with Q-Link pages and a bank browser.

**No factory sounds or samples of the instrument are included.** Put your own `.syx` sound or project dumps in `SYSEX/` inside the plugin folder (`/sdcard/Synths/sd88me - VST - Sturm-TP/`); the installer keeps `SYSEX/` and `SAMPLES/` across upgrades. The drum and percussion samples that ship are stand-ins generated by this project.

**Status:** release (0.1.1), tested on a Force; MPC OS 3.x only (the skin format). The analog parts are modelled from circuits and not yet compared with an instrument. CPU on the Force: about 26 % of one audio block at p99 with any number of voices; the Q-Link sweep reaches 37 % while stand-in samples are built in the background (FAIL by the bench's stress thresholds, fine for one or two instances).

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61). The installer refuses anything else.

manifest.name: SurgeXXL
manifest.about: Surge XT's synth engine (every factory patch and wavetable, your own patches and wavetables) as a native instrument for the Akai Force.

versions.notes:
**SurgeXXL 0.2.0** — Surge XT 1.3.4's synth engine as a native MPC OS instrument for the Force (MPC OS 3.x).

> **This is the fix for "SurgeXXL loads nothing / crashes MPC".** Every earlier version (0.1.0-0.1.3) failed at the very first step on a Force: MPC runs plugins with no `HOME` variable, Surge asked for it while starting, and no instance could be made (the crash log said `create: exception The environment variable HOME is unset or empty`). Fixed, and every offline test now runs without HOME, as MPC does.

Also new: built with the mpc-vst-plugins wrapper fix for Q-Links on the automation screen (UpdateDisplay, #486-#489).

Every Surge factory and third-party patch (3008) and wavetable (761), your own patches (SAVE) and wavetables (`/sdcard/SurgeXXL/Wavetables`), eight pages with Q-Links, every Surge effect except Spring Reverb (Airwindows included). See the README for the pages and folders.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61), **MPC OS 3.x** (the skin uses 3.x features).
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device, i.e. a modded unit. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.
- About 450 MB free on `/sdcard` (the patches and wavetables).

## Install it on its own

The package is about 450 MB unpacked. Install routes unpack a package in the device's `/tmp`, which on a Force is held in RAM, so **install SurgeXXL by itself, not in a batch with other plugins**, and save your project first. The scripted install below unpacks on the card instead and doesn't use RAM:

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the card: `scp -r SurgeXXL-0.2.0 root@<device-ip>:/sdcard/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /sdcard/SurgeXXL-0.2.0/install.sh`
3. Remove the copied folder afterwards: `ssh root@<device-ip> rm -rf /sdcard/SurgeXXL-0.2.0`

The installer stops MPC, copies the plugin folder into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds SurgeXXL to MPC's plugin list and starts MPC again. Installing over 0.1.3 replaces it. From 0.1.2 or older (the `ANDREALPHEUS - VST - SurgeXXL` folder): run that version's `uninstall.sh` first, or delete that folder, so its 450 MB doesn't stay on the card. Your own patches and wavetables in `/sdcard/SurgeXXL` are never touched.

Then add **SurgeXXL** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). To check it started: `cat /sdcard/SurgeXXL/surgexxl.log` ends with `ready: 3008 patches, 761 wavetables`.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /sdcard/SurgeXXL-0.2.0/uninstall.sh` (copy the folder over again if you removed it).

versions.notes:
TinyFreaky by MagicStino brings expressive **eight-voice synthesis** to Akai Force and MPC via OpenPlugin, plus Windows, macOS and Linux.

### Explore the sound

16 engines span detuned waves, wavetable and additive textures, plucked strings, virtual analog, waveshaping, FM, formants, chords, speech, modal resonance, noise and bass. Shape them with the **5×7 modulation matrix**, arpeggiator with rate/swing, and **64-step sequencer**.

### New in 0.4.0

The factory bank now has sound-informed TinyFreaky names: **Mouth Pop**, **Arp Bent Bark**, **Static Rise**, **Bass Drool** and more. Names reflect engine character, envelopes and movement. All **342 playable slots** retain their sound settings and slot IDs, so existing saved projects keep their sound. The 114 unavailable slots are labelled clearly.

[Complete old-to-new preset-name list](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky/blob/v0.4.0/docs/preset-name-changes-0.4.0.csv) · [Source and engine guide](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky)

### Downloads

- [Force / MPC ARMv7](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky/releases/download/v0.4.0/Tinyfreaky-0.4.0-mpc-armv7.zip)
- [Windows x64 VST3](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky/releases/download/v0.4.0/Tinyfreaky-0.4.0-Windows-VST3.zip)
- [macOS universal VST3](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky/releases/download/v0.4.0/Tinyfreaky-0.4.0-macOS-VST3.zip)
- [macOS universal Audio Unit](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky/releases/download/v0.4.0/Tinyfreaky-0.4.0-macOS-AU.zip)
- [Linux VST3](https://github.com/MagicStino/TinyFreaky/releases/download/v0.4.0/Tinyfreaky-0.4.0-Linux-VST3.zip)

### Validation and compatibility

Platform builds passed automated checks, including the Steinberg VST3 validator, Apple auval, engine/voice regression checks and the Force VST2 host contract. Local before/after checks confirm identical saved state and C4 audio across all 456 slots. Physical-device confirmation of 0.4.0 remains pending.

macOS builds are ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. Preset translation is approximate; six engine families and full sequence/sample payload support remain unavailable. See OpenPlugin for supported MPC device and firmware versions. Required third-party licenses and credits are included.
