manifest.name: Tributary
manifest.about: Sums chosen Elektron Overbridge outputs onto one MPC track. Heard on a Digitone II.

versions.notes:
One Tributary can sum the outputs you switch on, onto the MPC track it sits on.

The switches come from the connected machine. A Digitone II still shows MAIN, ACTIVE, 1–16, DLY, REV, CHO, and IN. A Digitakt, Syntakt, or the other listed machines show their own names. A fresh copy starts with Main on. An older project that saved a single source opens with only that output on, so leave Main off when you are splitting the machine across tracks.

The USB cushion is the one measured on a Digitone II: about 4 ms behind the newest sample, walked back gently when it drifts.

versions.notes:
Island and afro sounds - 128 presets and 65 instruments for afrobeat, amapiano, kompa, soca, reggae and Hawaiian music. Two layers, glide, scoop, vibrato, filter, drive, chorus, delay, reverb, nine colorways.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61).
  The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install (scripted)

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r Tropix-0.1.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/Tropix-0.1.1/install.sh`

The installer checks the device, **stops MPC** (save your project first), copies `portable/3dthc - VST - Tropix/` (the plugin, its skin
and its data, as one folder) into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds the plugin to MPC's plugin list from the
folder's `plugin-meta.xml` and starts MPC again. Running it again upgrades in place, keeping your own files.
An older install of this plugin (the previous layout, with the `.so` in `/sdcard/vst`) is replaced, not duplicated.
`-y` skips the confirmation prompt; `-t <folder>` installs into another Synths folder (for example on a card).

Then add **Tropix** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). Its screen appears in the plugin view,
and the Q-Links follow the page.

Full instructions, including installing by hand, are in `INSTALL.md` inside the zip.

manifest.name: Vibe FX
manifest.about: Drive, chorus, reverb and tape delay in one native MPC OS insert effect.

versions.notes:
A native **Akai MPC OS insert effect** — drive, chorus, reverb and tape delay in one slot, with a touchscreen skin and Q-Links. VST2 for MPC OS (armv7).

**Signal chain:** `IN → DRIVE → CHORUS → (dry) ─┬─ REVERB × send ─┐ └─ DELAY × send ─┴─ OUT`

- **Drive** — tape-style saturation front end
- **Chorus** — Juno-style stereo BBD chorus (rate / depth / mix)
- **Reverb** — FDN hall (decay, damping, high-pass, pre-delay) on its own send
- **Tape delay** — free or tempo-synced (dotted divisions), bipolar tone (LP ↔ feedback HP), feedback with a safety cap, on its own send

Two touchscreen pages (DRIVE / CHORUS and REVERB / DELAY) in the Mutable Instruments style, with a matching Q-Link map.

### Install
Download `Vibe-FX-0.9.0-mpc-armv7.zip`, unzip, and run `install.sh` (see `INSTALL.md`). Built with the [mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins) porting kit.

### Tested
MPC One (Gen1), firmware Hakai 3.9. Other Gen1 devices (Live / X / Key / Force) run the same program and are expected to work but are unverified. Gen2 is not supported.

MIT license.

versions.notes:
First release of **Xenia**, an emulation of the Microwave XT wavetable synthesizer for Akai MPC Gen2 standalone devices (MPC Live III and kin, aarch64, MPC OS 3.x), built on gearmulator's XT emulation.

**You need your own Microwave XT ROM.** None is included. After installing, put the 256 kB image (or its two 128 kB halves, or an OS update `.mid` next to a full ROM) in the plugin folder's `xenia/roms/` and restart the plugin.

**Install:** unzip, copy the folder to the device and run `sh install.sh` as root (`sh install.sh -t /nvme/Synths` on a Live III). It restarts MPC and backs up `MPC.settings`.

**What is in it:** ten touchscreen pages (PLAY, BANKS, OSC, AMP & ARP, FILTER, ENV & LFO, WAVE ENV, MOD, SLOTS 1-8, SLOTS 9-16), the two ROM banks with a patch browser, four assignable play knobs, the effect, Q-Link sub-pages so every knob has a Q-Link, and PANIC / INIT PATCH.

**Tested:** one MPC Live III, MPC OS 3.9.1.2, 2026-10-27: loads, boots in about half a second, plays, bank and preset steppers, BANKS tiles, data wheel, Q-Link sub-pages and option popups work; the emulator thread uses about 35% of one core with no dropouts.

**Not verified yet:** saving and reloading a project, INIT PATCH, long sessions, and the output level against other instruments (GAIN defaults to 250%). One part in Multi mode only: the XT's multi, wave editor and Global menu are not exposed. Gen1 devices and the Force are not supported.

# Downloads — choose your architecture

| **Gen1 / Force** | **ARM32 (ARMv7)** | [Download Gen1 / ARM32](https://github.com/timomacquis/piClideaN16-MPC/releases/download/v1.3.0/piClideaN-MPC-1.3.0-armv7.zip) |

Both packages are version **1.3.0**. Gen1 / Force remains unchanged and device-validated. **Gen2 1.3.0 is pending device testing**, with offline build/package checks passed. The original 1.2.4 port was tested on MPC Live III by Thomas Phillips; other Gen2 models are untested.

[Gen2 installation](https://github.com/timomacquis/piClideaN16-MPC/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION-GEN2.md) · [Validation details](https://github.com/timomacquis/piClideaN16-MPC/blob/main/docs/GEN2-VALIDATION.md)

The separate `ClideaN-MPC-1.3.0-mpc-armv7.zip` asset is the standard catalog package for Gen1; it is also unchanged.

---

# Version 1.3.0

- Add Random Walk, Random Loop and Bounce to the eleven-shape MOD palette.
- Add pulse width, random step size, loop evolution, gravity and restitution controls.
- Chain either LFO into the other’s rate, depth or offset. Preserve the existing NOTE ON and threshold behavior.
- Cache static waveform previews and compute them on a dedicated background worker.
- Reduce queued display notification bursts and remove unused preview notifications.
- Share identical image assets and streamline the miniature steps on both track pages.
- Correct native miniature frame slicing and retain note, custom-value and playhead colours.
- Update the illustrated user manual.

Musical operation and interface improvements were validated by the user on Akai Force. Crackles previously reported during interaction were no longer observed in the tested setup. CPU and effects loads vary by project; no universal performance guarantee is made.

Projects save the PICN7 state format; PICN6 states can be loaded. Earlier plugin versions cannot load the new state format. Parameter indices remain unchanged.
